text: Greco had not yet realized the importance of keeping control of the centre and gives Black this weak move instead of the correct 6... d6.
zh: 格雷科还没有认识到保持中心控制的重要性，给黑方安排了这步软着，而不是正确的6... d6。

text: This is even stronger than 8. cxd4.¹
zh: 这甚至比8. cxd4更强。¹

text: ¹ As we shall see, this comment is incorrect. After 8. cxd4 White has a clear advantage, since Black has no compensation for White's central control. The move 8. e5 is a mistake which gives Black at least equality.
zh: ¹ 正如后面将看到的，这个评注不正确。8. cxd4之后，白方明显有利，因为黑方没有足够的补偿来抵消白方的中心控制。8. e5是错误，至少让黑方取得均势。

caption_zh: 黑方走完8... Ng4后的局面

text: 9. cxd4?
zh: 9. cxd4?

text: Weakly played. By 9. Bg5 (an intermediate move!) 9... Qe8 10. cxd4 White would have obtained a winning position. (Greco and other authors right up to the middle of the nineteenth century did not see the intermediate move 9. Bg5, so that 8. e5 came to be regarded in the textbooks as a mistake!¹)
zh: 这步走得弱。9. Bg5——一记过渡着！——9... Qe8 10. cxd4本来可以使白方获得胜势。（格雷科以及此后直到十九世纪中叶的其他作者，都没有看到9. Bg5这记过渡着，因此教科书反而把8. e5视为错误！¹）

text: ¹ Black should meet 9. Bg5 by 9... dxc3!. After 10. Bxe7 Bxf2+ 11. Kf1 cxb2 12. Nc3 (12. Na3 Bxe1 also favours Black) 12... Bxe1 (12... bxa1=Q 13. Qxa1 Bxe1 14. Nd5 is unclear) 13. Nd5 Nxe7 14. Nxe7+ Kh8 Black has a clear advantage in view of the threats of 15... bxa1=Q and 15... Ne3+. White's strongest move is 9. b4!, but an analysis of the resulting complications (which lead to a roughly equal position) would take us too far afield. Perhaps those old analysts knew a thing or two after all!
zh: ¹ 黑方应以9... dxc3!应对9. Bg5。10. Bxe7 Bxf2+ 11. Kf1 cxb2 12. Nc3（12. Na3 Bxe1也对黑方有利）12... Bxe1（12... bxa1=Q 13. Qxa1 Bxe1 14. Nd5不明朗）13. Nd5 Nxe7 14. Nxe7+ Kh8之后，由于威胁15... bxa1=Q和15... Ne3+，黑方明显有利。白方最强的是9. b4!，但分析由此产生的复杂变化——其结果大致均势——会离题太远。也许那些老分析家终究还是有些真本事！

text: 9... Nxd4! 10. Nxd4 Qh4
zh: 9... Nxd4! 10. Nxd4 Qh4

text: This is Greco's trick. White has two exposed spots, at h2 and f2.
zh: 这就是格雷科的技巧。白方有两个暴露的点：h2和f2。

text: Greco naturally also gives the continuation 11. Nf3 Qxf2+ followed by 12... Qg1+ and a smothered mate by the knight at f2.
zh: 格雷科自然也给出11. Nf3 Qxf2+，随后12... Qg1+，由马在f2完成闷杀的后续手段。

text: In carrying his attack further Greco does not notice all the finesses. 12... Nxe3+ followed by ...d6 would have been better here.²
zh: 继续进攻时，格雷科没有注意到所有细节。这里12... Nxe3+后接...d6本来更好。²

text: ² A baffling comment, as after 12... Nxe3+ 13. fxe3 d6 14. Nf3 White starts to consolidate his extra material. Greco's continuation appears best to me.
zh: ² 这个评注令人费解，因为12... Nxe3+ 13. fxe3 d6 14. Nf3之后，白方开始巩固自己的子力优势。我认为格雷科的后续手段反而最好。

text: 13. Ke2 Qxg2 14. Rg1 Nxe3 15. Kxe3?
zh: 13. Ke2 Qxg2 14. Rg1 Nxe3 15. Kxe3?

text: This way White loses two valuable pawns, and Greco concludes his analysis with 15... Bxd4+ 16. Kxd4 Qxf2+ 17. Kc3 Qe3+ 18. Bd3 Qxe5+, with advantage to Black.
zh: 这样白方丢掉两个重要的兵。格雷科以15... Bxd4+ 16. Kxd4 Qxf2+ 17. Kc3 Qe3+ 18. Bd3 Qxe5+结束分析，黑方有利。

text: Instead of 15. Kxe3?, the correct continuation is 15. Rxg2 Nxd1 16. Nf5, when Black must find the reply 16... d5! 17. Nxg7 Bh3!, if he is to retain the better prospects (though even here there is still some uncertainty after 18. Rg3 Bxf2 19. Rxh3 dxc4 20. Nd2, etc.). If he played 16... Nxb2 17. Nh6+ Kh8 18. Nxf7+, he would have to consent to a draw, since 18... Rxf7 is probably not a good idea.³
zh: 白方不应15. Kxe3?，正确的后续手段是15. Rxg2 Nxd1 16. Nf5。黑方若想保持较好的前景，必须找到16... d5! 17. Nxg7 Bh3!这个应对；不过即使如此，18. Rg3 Bxf2 19. Rxh3 dxc4 20. Nd2等之后，局面仍有些不确定。如果黑方16... Nxb2 17. Nh6+ Kh8 18. Nxf7+，就不得不接受和棋，因为18... Rxf7很可能并非好主意。³

text: ³ After 18... Rxf7 19. Bxf7 b6!, followed by ...Ba6+ and developing the rook, Black is virtually winning – three pawns for the exchange and a pair of active bishops is surely too much.
zh: ³ 18... Rxf7 19. Bxf7 b6!之后，再接...Ba6+并出动车，黑方实际上已经是胜势：以半子为代价换得三兵，再加上一对活跃的双象，补偿显然十分充足。

text: In step with the general advance in chess skill there can also be seen an advance in the technique of attacking the castled king, first with Philidor and then, particularly, with Morphy. The romantic reaction which followed led to the development of a number of particular types of sacrificial attacks, but without in general reaching Morphy's level. Steinitz was concerned with perfecting defensive technique, and his influence on the style of the period was slowly beginning to make the attack on the castled king fade from master chess. Lasker, too, the new World Champion, was even in his youth already turning away from forcing such attacks, preferring to aim at perfection in the endgame.
zh: 随着整体棋艺的提高，攻击王城的技术也在进步，先是菲利多尔，后来尤其是墨菲。随后兴起的浪漫派反响，推动了多种特殊弃子进攻的发展，但总体上没有达到墨菲的水平。斯坦尼茨致力于完善防守技术；他对时代棋风的影响，逐渐使王城进攻在大师对局中淡出。新任世界冠军拉斯克甚至在年轻时，就已不再执意强行发动这种进攻，而更倾向于追求残局中的精确。

text: At the end of the century, however, there were three great masters who defended the thesis of attacking chess and who in doing so clearly showed themselves to be supporters of the attack on the castled king. These were Chigorin, Tarrasch and Pillsbury, each of whom in his own way helped to enrich the technique of attack. Chigorin illustrated particularly the power of the positional sacrifice in his games; Tarrasch's thesis was that the rapid development of the pieces and a strong centre were the basic requisites for an attack on the castled king; while Pillsbury created a kind of synthesis of the attacking style and the positional and endgame play of Steinitz and Lasker. In other words, the American grandmaster showed how a rapid switch can be made from attack to a simplification which gives the better ending.
zh: 然而，十九世纪末有三位大棋手坚持进攻型国际象棋的主张，并明确支持攻击王城。他们是齐果林、塔拉什和皮尔斯伯里，各自以不同方式丰富了进攻技术。齐果林的对局尤其展示了位置性弃子的威力；塔拉什认为，迅速出子和强大的中心，是攻击王城的基本条件；皮尔斯伯里则把进攻棋风，与斯坦尼茨、拉斯克的位置战和残局技巧融为一体。换句话说，这位美国大棋手展示了怎样从进攻迅速转入简化，并获得更好的残局。

text: In this way all the basic elements of a perfected technique for attacking the castled king were set out, and after a short period of stagnation in the first two decades of the present century there followed the real blossoming of the dynamic style with the arrival of Capablanca and Alekhine. This development is still relevant to the theme of the attack on the castled king today, and more will be said about it at the end of the book.
zh: 至此，完善的王城进攻技术所需的各项基本要素都已具备。二十世纪头二十年经历短暂的停滞后，随着卡帕布兰卡和阿廖欣的到来，动态棋风真正繁荣起来。这种发展，在作者写作时仍与攻击王城的主题密切相关；本书末尾还将进一步讨论。

text: 4 Mating patterns
zh: 第四章　将杀模式

text: Spatial relationships in a mating attack can be observed by examining mating patterns, focal-points, and the roles played by the ranks, files, and diagonals. In this chapter we shall be concerned with mating patterns. This choice has a practical justification in that mating patterns can be more easily remembered than the ways leading up to mate. For this reason mating patterns, even though they occur only at the very end of a mating attack, are fundamental for practical purposes because of the excellent mnemonic assistance which they provide to the player.
zh: 通过考察将杀模式、杀王焦点，以及横线、纵线和斜线的作用，可以认识将杀进攻中的空间关系。本章讨论将杀模式。这样安排有实际理由：与通往将杀的具体走法相比，将杀模式更容易记住。因此，虽然将杀模式只在进攻的最后阶段出现，但它能为棋手提供极好的记忆线索，在实战中具有基础性的重要意义。

text: Our first concern is for the most common mating patterns; these hardly ever occur in the middle of the board, but they are very frequent in the castling area, i.e. near the king's position on the edge of the board.
zh: 我们先讨论最常见的将杀模式。它们很少出现在棋盘中央，却经常出现在王城区域，也就是靠近棋盘边缘的王的位置附近。

text: Typical mates without enemy pieces
zh: 没有其他敌方子力的典型将杀

text: There are a very large number of typical mates of this kind and most of them are elementary, so we shall consider only a few examples. (For the sake of greater clarity the diagrams are shown without the white king.)
zh: 这类典型将杀很多，大多属于基本知识，因此只看几个例子。为了让图示更清楚，图中省去了白王。

text: In the first position White, to move, has a choice between two typical mates:
zh: 第一个局面中，轮到白方行棋，他可以选择两种典型将杀：

text: In this position there are again two possible mates, depending on how Black replies.
zh: 这个局面同样有两种将杀，取决于黑方怎样应对。

text: If **1. Nf6+ Kh8**, then **2. Rh7#** (the so-called Arab mate, because it is recorded in Arabic manuscripts of the ninth century). If **1. Nf6+ Kf8**, then there follows **2. Rf7#**, a mating pattern which is worth remembering.
zh: 如果**1. Nf6+ Kh8**，则**2. Rh7#**。这就是所谓的阿拉伯杀，因为九世纪的阿拉伯手稿中已经记载了它。如果**1. Nf6+ Kf8**，则**2. Rf7#**；这个将杀模式也值得记住。

text: Another mate which should be known is this one with two knights, but if there are no other pieces on the board then it cannot be forced.
zh: 另一个应该熟悉的将杀，是这个双马将杀；但如果棋盘上没有其他子力，就无法强制实现。

text: Typical mates with enemy pieces
zh: 有其他敌方子力的典型将杀

text: The so-called back-row mate by the rook (or queen) is one of the most typical mating patterns.
zh: 由车或后完成的所谓底线杀，是最典型的将杀模式之一。

text: Of the fairly large number of typical mates with queen and pawn this one is given first.
zh: 后与兵配合的典型将杀有很多，这里先看这一种。

text: Black is to move; he cannot escape mate, since he is threatened by **1. Qh6** and **2. Qg7#**. If he plays 1... Kh7, then **2. Qh4+** and **3. Qh6**, etc. If Black had a pawn on h7 he would have the defence 1... Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8.
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，但他无法逃脱将杀，因为白方威胁**1. Qh6**后接**2. Qg7#**。如果1... Kh7，则**2. Qh4+**后接**3. Qh6**等。如果黑方在h7还有一个兵，就可以用1... Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8防守。

text: Damiano's Mate
zh: 达米亚诺杀

text: This is a position from the book (1512) by Damiano, a Portuguese apothecary, one of the first authors in the literature of European chess. White mates in five moves.
zh: 这个局面出自葡萄牙药剂师达米亚诺1512年的著作。他是欧洲国际象棋文献最早的一批作者之一。白方有五步杀。

text: 1. Rh8+ Kxh8 2. Rh1+ Kg8 3. Rh8+ Kxh8 4. Qh1+ Kg8 5. Qh7#
zh: 1. Rh8+ Kxh8 2. Rh1+ Kg8 3. Rh8+ Kxh8 4. Qh1+ Kg8 5. Qh7#

text: The rook sacrifices were naturally introduced to make the essential point clear: the queen must reach the h-file with gain of tempo.
zh: 安排这两次弃车，自然是为了突出关键：后必须带着先手进入h线。

text: The pattern of Damiano's mate can be seen more clearly in the following examples.
zh: 下面的例子可以更清楚地展示达米亚诺杀的模式。

text: 1. Qh5 Be7 2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#
zh: 1. Qh5 Be7 2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#

text: In this case a bishop has been placed on f8 and also a pawn on d6, with the result that the bishop can only move to e7, where it blocks the king's escape. The general theme of Damiano's mate, the pattern of which is characterized by a black pawn on g7 and a white pawn or bishop on g6, can be subjected to numerous variations.
zh: 这个例子中，f8放了一只象，d6还放了一个兵；因此黑象只能走到e7，在那里堵住黑王的退路。达米亚诺杀的一般主题，以g7黑兵和g6白兵或白象为特征，可以形成许多不同的变化。

text: The following diagram serves as a memory aid for mates with queen and rook:
zh: 下图可以帮助记忆后与车配合的将杀：

text: Black, to move, cannot avoid mate; if he plays 1... Kg7, then **2. Qh6+** and **3. Qh7#** or **3. Qh8#**, while if 1... f6, then **2. Qh7#**. If Black has another pawn on g7 he can save himself from immediate mate by 1... f6, while if he has one on g6 he can extricate himself by 1... Kg7.
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，但他无法避免将杀。如果1... Kg7，则**2. Qh6+**后接**3. Qh7#**或**3. Qh8#**；如果1... f6，则**2. Qh7#**。如果黑方在g7还有一个兵，可以用1... f6避免立即被杀；如果在g6有一个兵，则可以1... Kg7脱身。

text: Of the mates with queen and bishop this position is worth remembering.
zh: 在后与象配合的将杀中，这个局面值得记住。

text: Black cannot save himself from mate, but if he plays 1... g6, White does not reply 2. Bxg6+ (which is answered by 2... Kg7, and Black's king slips away) but 2. Qh6, in which case there is no remedy against mate.
zh: 黑方无法避免将杀，但如果他1... g6，白方不应2. Bxg6+，因为2... Kg7后黑王会逃走；应当2. Qh6，这样黑方就无法防住将杀。

text: Smothered Mate
zh: 闷杀

text: The smothered mate with queen and knight is a celebrated one: **1. Nf7+ Kg8 2. Nh6+ Kh8** (or 2... Kf8 3. Qf7#) **3. Qg8+! Rxg8** (or 3... Nxg8) **4. Nf7#**.
zh: 后与马配合的闷杀十分著名：**1. Nf7+ Kg8 2. Nh6+ Kh8**（或2... Kf8 3. Qf7#）**3. Qg8+! Rxg8**（或3... Nxg8）**4. Nf7#**。

text: This position falls into the category of typical mates, and it is useful to know the mating patterns which arise if Black tries to parry the threat of Qh7#, e.g. with **1... Rb8**.
zh: 这个局面也属于典型将杀。黑方如果设法应付Qh7#的威胁，例如走**1... Rb8**，熟悉随后可能出现的将杀模式很有用。

text: If there is a black pawn on e7 or if the square is otherwise occupied by Black, then there follows **2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#**; if this is not so, mate can be achieved, for example, by **2. Qxf7+ Kh8 3. Ne6 Rg8 4. Qh5#**.
zh: 如果e7有一个黑兵，或被其他黑子占据，就有**2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#**；如果不是这样，也能将杀，例如**2. Qxf7+ Kh8 3. Ne6 Rg8 4. Qh5#**。

text: Of the various attacking positions with queen and knight this scheme is also well worth remembering.
zh: 在后与马配合的各种进攻阵形中，这种阵形也很值得记住。

text: On **1. Nf6+**, Black replies 1... Kh8 and if 2. Nh5+, then 2... f6. If **1... Kg7**, White has a double check with **2. Ne8+** (in some cases, depending on the arrangement of the other pieces, 2. Nh5+ may be stronger) and after 2... Kh6 **3. Qf4+** g5 **4. Qf6+** Kh5 **5. Ng7+** White only needs a pawn on g2 or h2 to force mate.
zh: 对**1. Nf6+**，黑方应以1... Kh8；如果2. Nh5+，则2... f6。如果**1... Kg7**，白方可以**2. Ne8+**双将；在某些局面中，根据其他子力的配置，2. Nh5+可能更强。随后2... Kh6 **3. Qf4+** g5 **4. Qf6+** Kh5 **5. Ng7+**，白方只需在g2或h2有一个兵，就能强制将杀。

text: Greco's Mate
zh: 格雷科杀

text: This position is also worth knowing; Black is forced to play **1... h6**, after which he is mated by **2. Bxf7+ Kh8 3. Qg6! hxg5 4. Qh5#**.
zh: 这个局面也值得熟悉。黑方被迫走**1... h6**，随后**2. Bxf7+ Kh8 3. Qg6! hxg5 4. Qh5#**，白方将杀。

text: In the case of mating patterns with rook and bishop one should first of all get to know the above position.
zh: 研究车与象配合的将杀模式，首先应熟悉这个局面。

text: It is Black's move and he must try to parry Rg5#; this cannot be achieved by 1... h6, because of 2. Rxh6, which leaves him with no way out. So **1... Rc8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7!**, and now too mate is unavoidable, for Black is unable to free the square d7 in time to provide the king with an escape square. If he did not have, for instance, the pawn on c6, he could play 3... Bc6 4. Rxh7 Ke8 and then 5. Rh8+ could be met by 5... Kd7. One could replace Black's bishop and c6-pawn by a white pawn on c6 and a black one on c7; mate would still be unavoidable.¹
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，他必须设法防住Rg5#。1... h6做不到，因为2. Rxh6后仍无路可逃。因此**1... Rc8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7!**，但将杀依旧无法避免：黑方不能及时腾出d7，为王提供逃脱格。例如，如果没有c6兵，他就能3... Bc6 4. Rxh7 Ke8，再以5... Kd7应对5. Rh8+。也可以把黑象和c6黑兵换成c6白兵和c7黑兵；将杀仍然不可避免。¹

text: ¹ In the diagram position, Black can avoid mate by 1... Ra8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7 Ra4 4. Rxh7 Rg4. It is true to say that this defence is not often available in practical situations, but it is worth bearing in mind the idea of “defending from behind” because it is often overlooked.
zh: ¹ 在图中局面，黑方可以用1... Ra8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7 Ra4 4. Rxh7 Rg4避免将杀。实战中确实不常有这种防守，但值得记住“从后方防守”的思路，因为它经常被忽略。

text: Morphy's Mate
zh: 墨菲杀

text: The pattern of this mate with rook and bishop becomes clear in its final stage.
zh: 这种车象将杀的模式，在最后阶段便清楚地显现出来。

text: 1. Qxf6 gxf6 2. Rg1+ Kh8 3. Bxf6#
zh: 1. Qxf6 gxf6 2. Rg1+ Kh8 3. Bxf6#

text: Morphy's Concealed Mate
zh: 隐蔽的墨菲杀

text: A similar mating pattern occurs in this diagram: **1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rxf7+** (not 2. Rg1+ because of 2... f6) **2... Kg8 3. Rg7+ Kh8 4. Rg1+ Rf6 5. Bxf6#**.
zh: 这个图中出现了类似的将杀模式：**1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rxf7+**（不能2. Rg1+，因为2... f6）**2... Kg8 3. Rg7+ Kh8 4. Rg1+ Rf6 5. Bxf6#**。

text: **1. Rd8+ Kf7** (or 1... Kh7 2. Rh8#) **2. Rf8#** is a typical mating pattern well worth remembering.
zh: **1. Rd8+ Kf7**（或1... Kh7 2. Rh8#）**2. Rf8#**，是一个很值得记住的典型将杀模式。

text: Anastasia's Mate
zh: 阿纳斯塔西娅杀

text: 1. Ne7+ Kh8 2. Rxh7+ Kxh7 3. Rh5#
zh: 1. Ne7+ Kh8 2. Rxh7+ Kxh7 3. Rh5#

text: (The name comes from W. Heinse's novel Anastasia and chess (1803), in which this mate is recorded.)
zh: 这个名称来自W.海因泽1803年的小说《阿纳斯塔西娅与国际象棋》，书中记载了这种将杀。

text: Here the continuation ends with a typical mating pattern with a rook and pawn.
zh: 这里的后续手段，最终形成车与兵配合的典型将杀模式。

text: 1. Qg5 Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8 3. Qxh7+ Kxh7 4. Rh1#
zh: 1. Qg5 Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8 3. Qxh7+ Kxh7 4. Rh1#

text: “Blind swine”
zh: “盲猪”

text: If it is White's move, he mates with **1. Rg7+**, **2. Rh7+**, and **3. Rbg7#**. If Black is to move and plays **1... Rfd8**, White can neither force mate nor even win. That is to say, after 2. Rg7+ Kh8 3. Rh7+ Kg8 4. Rbg7+ Kf8 5. Rb7, Black simply plays 5... Kg8, “questioning” the white rook and countering the threat of mate.
zh: 如果轮到白方，他可以**1. Rg7+**、**2. Rh7+**、**3. Rbg7#**将杀。如果轮到黑方，且他走**1... Rfd8**，白方不仅无法强制将杀，甚至不能获胜。也就是说，2. Rg7+ Kh8 3. Rh7+ Kg8 4. Rbg7+ Kf8 5. Rb7之后，黑方只需5... Kg8，攻击白车，同时应付将杀威胁。

text: (It depends of course on the distribution of the other pieces whether White can in fact win. In this position he can easily mate if he has a pawn on h4, for he plays 6. h5 followed by 7. h6, 8. Rbg7+, and 9. Rh8# – a mate which is worth remembering. In this line Black's pawn on f6 is actually a help to White. If it were not there, Black could get a draw after 6. h5 by playing 6... Ra6!.)
zh: 当然，白方究竟能否取胜，还取决于其他子力的配置。在这个局面中，如果白方在h4有一个兵，就能轻松将杀：6. h5后接7. h6、8. Rbg7+和9. Rh8#，这是值得记住的将杀。这个变化中，黑方的f6兵实际上帮了白方的忙；如果没有它，6. h5之后黑方可以6... Ra6!取得和棋。

text: The pair of rooks which “grunt out check” on the seventh rank but cannot get a sight of mate were once nicknamed “blind swine” by Janowski.
zh: 两只车在第七横线上哼哼着不断将军，却看不到将杀的机会，雅诺夫斯基曾给它们起了个绰号：“盲猪”。

text: An acquaintance with typical mating patterns is extremely useful when making a quick survey of the board in an actual game. The addition of further material to the position can be especially useful, for then one can see which changes help to prevent mate and which enrich the mating patterns in new situations.
zh: 实战中快速审视棋盘时，熟悉典型将杀模式极其有用。在这些局面中加入其他子力，尤其有助于学习：这样可以看清，哪些变化有助于防止将杀，哪些变化又会在新局面中丰富将杀模式。

text: Less usual mating patterns
zh: 不太常见的将杀模式

text: Of the large number of less usual, and even exotic, mating patterns, I have chosen ones which bear some nickname or which can easily be given one.
zh: 不太常见、甚至十分奇异的将杀模式很多。我选出了一些已经有绰号，或很容易起绰号的模式。

text: Epaulette Mate
zh: 肩章杀

text: The epaulettes are, of course, the two black rooks on the king's shoulders. The next mate also gets its name from its outward appearance.
zh: 所谓肩章，当然就是王两肩上的那两只黑车。下一个将杀也根据外形得名。

text: “Swallow's tail”
zh: “燕尾杀”

text: Pawn Mate
zh: 兵杀

text: **1. g6 Bg8 2. g7#**. On 1. g6 Kg8 2. Qxh7+ Kf8 we get yet another mating pattern with 3. g7+ Kf7 4. g8=Q# (mate with two queens).
zh: **1. g6 Bg8 2. g7#**。如果1. g6 Kg8 2. Qxh7+ Kf8，则3. g7+ Kf7 4. g8=Q#，又得到另一种将杀模式——双后将杀。

text: Mate with Two Bishops
zh: 双象将杀

text: **1. Be6** d4 **2. Bh2** and **3. Be5#**. This could also be called Rubinstein's mate, after the famous game Rotlewi–Rubinstein, in which mate with two bishops was the basic motif of the attack.
zh: **1. Be6** d4 **2. Bh2**，随后**3. Be5#**。这种将杀也可以称为鲁宾斯坦杀：著名的罗特莱维对鲁宾斯坦一局中，双象将杀正是进攻的基本主题。

text: Boden's Mate
zh: 博登杀
caption_zh: 舒尔德（白）对博登（黑），黑方行棋

text: This position is from the game Schulder–Boden, London 1853¹, in which the following mate with two bishops was recorded for the first time; it is not uncommon after castling queenside. Black plays: **1... Qxc3+! 2. bxc3 Ba3#**.
zh: 这是1853年在伦敦的舒尔德对博登一局中的局面¹，也是这种双象将杀第一次见诸记录；长易位后，这种将杀并不少见。黑方走：**1... Qxc3+! 2. bxc3 Ba3#**。

text: ¹ In the original book this example was incorrectly given as Macdonell–Boden, 1869 and Black's rook on e8 was missing.
zh: ¹ 原著误把这个例子写成1869年的麦克唐纳对博登，而且漏掉了e8的黑车。

text: Pillsbury's Mate
zh: 皮尔斯伯里杀

text: **1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rg8+! Kxg8 3. Rg1+** and mate. This is really a variation on Morphy's mate, contrived in such a way that it is the rook which mates and not the bishop, which is under attack from Black's rook.
zh: **1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rg8+! Kxg8 3. Rg1+**，随后将杀。这实际上是墨菲杀的一种变化：由于白象受到黑车攻击，安排成由车而非象来完成将杀。

text: Legall's Mate
zh: 莱加尔杀

text: Legall was Philidor's teacher and this position arose in the game Legall–St Brie, Paris 1750. The moves leading up to the diagram were **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. Bc4 Bg4 4. Nc3 g6?** and Legall now played:
zh: 莱加尔是菲利多尔的老师。这个局面出现在1750年巴黎的莱加尔对圣布里一局中。图前走法是**1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. Bc4 Bg4 4. Nc3 g6?**，随后莱加尔走了：
caption_zh: 黑方走完4... g6后的局面

text: **5. Nxe5! Bxd1?** (5... Be6 would have been better) **6. Bxf7+ Ke7 7. Nd5#**. (This is of course a case of an attack before castling, but the example is given here for purely practical reasons.)
zh: **5. Nxe5! Bxd1?**（5... Be6更好）**6. Bxf7+ Ke7 7. Nd5#**。当然，这是易位前的进攻，但出于实用考虑，仍在这里列出。

text: The next mate is similar to Greco's, but differs in that the attacker (here Black) opens the h-file not only for his opponent but also for himself. It arose in the game Anderssen–Max Lange, Breslau 1859 after **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nd4 4. Nxd4 exd4 5. Bc4 Nf6 6. e5 d5 7. Bb3 Bg4 8. f3 Ne4 9. O-O d3 10. fxg4?**¹ (D).
zh: 下一种将杀与格雷科杀相似，区别在于进攻方——这里是黑方——打开h线时，不仅让对手能使用这条线，自己也能使用它。这种将杀出现在1859年布雷斯劳的安德森对马克斯·朗格一局中，经过**1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nd4 4. Nxd4 exd4 5. Bc4 Nf6 6. e5 d5 7. Bb3 Bg4 8. f3 Ne4 9. O-O d3 10. fxg4?**¹后，得到下图。
caption_zh: 白方走完10. fxg4后的局面

text: Max Lange's Mate
zh: 马克斯·朗格杀

text: ¹ 10. Qe1! would have favoured White.
zh: ¹ 10. Qe1!本来可以使白方有利。

text: Play proceeded as follows: **10... Bc5+ 11. Kh1 Ng3+ 12. hxg3 Qg5 13. Rf5 h5!** and now if 14. Rxg5, then 14... hxg4+ and mate; in the game White played **14. gxh5** but resigned after **14... Qxf5 15. g4 Qf2 0-1**.
zh: 对局接着这样进行：**10... Bc5+ 11. Kh1 Ng3+ 12. hxg3 Qg5 13. Rf5 h5!**。现在如果14. Rxg5，则14... hxg4+后将杀。实战中白方走**14. gxh5**，但在**14... Qxf5 15. g4 Qf2 0-1**之后认输。

text: The next position arose in the game Réti–Tartakower, Vienna 1910 after the moves **1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Qd3 e5 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O Nxe4** (D).
zh: 下一局面来自1910年在维也纳的列蒂对塔塔科维尔一局。经过**1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Qd3 e5 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O Nxe4**后，得到下图。
caption_zh: 黑方走完8... Nxe4后的局面

text: Réti's Mate
zh: 列蒂杀

text: The game concluded: **9. Qd8+! Kxd8 10. Bg5+ Kc7** (or 10... Ke8 11. Rd8#) **11. Bd8#**.
Blackburne's Mate
zh: 布莱克本杀

text: For this mate the attacker needs three minor pieces (two bishops and a knight) and usually a queen as well, which is sacrificed.
zh: 实现这种将杀，进攻方需要三个轻子——双象和一马——通常还需要一个后，用来弃掉。

text: **1. Qh1 h5 2. Qxh5! gxh5 3. Bh7#**. This mating pattern is named after Blackburne, who was the first to mate in this way.
zh: **1. Qh1 h5 2. Qxh5! gxh5 3. Bh7#**。这种将杀模式以首先采用它完成将杀的布莱克本命名。

text: 5 Focal-points
zh: 第五章　杀王焦点

text: The series of examples examined in the chapter on mating patterns has given us a good idea of the difficulties a defender encounters when his forces (especially the pawns in front of his castled king) are poorly placed and when the attacker's one aim is to fill the various 'holes and cracks' in the weakened enemy defences with his own pieces and thus obtain an even tighter grip. It follows from this that the squares in the immediate vicinity of the king, where the drama of the mating attack usually reaches its climax, play a special role. If the attacker threatens mate or actually mates on these squares, they are mating focal-points, but if he only harries the king from them or uses them as points from which to break into the castled position, they are called strategic or auxiliary focal-points. It may be that there is more than one mating focal-point, and in that case we speak of compound focal-points. If there are many focal-points (both mating and strategic) on squares of the same colour, we speak of a network of weak squares.
zh: 上一章关于将杀模式的一系列例子，已经让我们充分认识到：当防守方的子力，尤其是王城前的兵，位置不佳，而进攻方一心用自己的棋子填入对方防线中的各种“孔洞与裂缝”，不断加强控制时，防守方会遇到怎样的困难。因此，紧邻王的那些格子具有特殊作用；杀王的战斗通常就在这里达到高潮。如果进攻方威胁在这些格子上将杀，或者实际在这里将杀，它们就是将杀焦点；如果进攻方只是从这里骚扰王，或以此为突破王城的据点，它们就称为战略焦点或辅助焦点。有时将杀焦点不止一个，我们便称之为复合焦点。如果同一颜色的格子上存在许多焦点，无论是将杀焦点还是战略焦点，我们便称之为弱格网络。

text: Generally speaking, every focal-point is a weak square in the defender's territory and a potentially strong one for the attacker. In addition to the focal-points there are also other squares in the castling area which have a specific function, e.g. blocked squares, particularly those occupied by the defender's pawns, and also any weak squares on which the attacker can safely post his pieces.
zh: 一般而言，每一个焦点都是防守方阵地中的弱格，对进攻方则可能成为强格。王城区域中除焦点外，还有一些格子具有特定作用，例如被堵住的格子，尤其是防守方的兵占据的格子；还有一些弱格，进攻方可以安全地把棋子安置在那里。

text: As an illustration of this, take the following position (which we have already seen earlier). Here we have the following scheme:
zh: 以下局面前面已经出现过，我们用它来说明上述概念。各格的作用如下：

将杀格：g8、f8；
将杀焦点：h7、h8；
辅助焦点：h7（黑方用...Be7应对将杀威胁之后）；
进攻方的强格：f7、g6、h7；
被堵住的格子：g7，以及稍后的e7。

text: The focal-point at g7
zh: g7焦点

text: As usual, when referring to specific squares we assume that White is the attacker. It is understood that if Black is the attacker, then the discussion applies equally to the square g2.
zh: 和往常一样，讨论具体格子时，我们假定白方是进攻方。如果黑方发动进攻，下文的讨论同样适用于g2格。

text: The most important focal-points where castling kingside is concerned are g7 and h7, since these squares are more accessible to the attacker than the others in the castling area. Of the two, h7 is the more frequent object of attack (since it comes under fire from the bishop operating from d3, a natural point of development, while the king's knight can reach g5, for example, more easily than f5 or h5). However, attacks against g7 are the more dangerous. The reasons for this are very simple: the queen can mate more easily from g7 than h7 (owing to the king's ability to flee to f8), but as well as this, a weakness on g7 usually brings with it two more on f6 and h6, while one on h7 generally only entails a single extra one at g6. Every player of any experience is well acquainted with this fact and knows that ...g6 involves a greater weakening than ...h6. On the other hand, h7 is usually harder to defend than g7, which the king's bishop can support in two ways (from f8 or f6).
zh: 对短易位的王来说，最重要的焦点是g7和h7，因为进攻方比起王城区域中的其他格子，更容易接近这两格。其中，h7更常成为攻击目标：象从自然的出子位置d3便能攻击h7，而王翼马也更容易跳到g5，而不是f5或h5。不过，对g7的攻击更危险。原因很简单：后在g7比在h7更容易将杀，因为面对h7的后，王可能逃到f8；此外，g7的弱点通常还伴随着f6和h6两个弱点，而h7的弱点一般只会额外带来g6一个弱点。稍有经验的棋手都熟悉这一点，知道...g6对局面的削弱比...h6更大。另一方面，h7通常比g7更难防守；黑格象可以从f8或f6两个位置保护g7。

text: The next position illustrates a typical example of an action against the square g7:
zh: 下一局面是针对g7格展开行动的典型例子：

text: White, to play, has excellent prospects for an attack on g7. His knight is already observing the square, while his queen and bishop are in a position to threaten it in one move. An extremely useful point is the fact that the queen has the choice of attacking from either c3 or g3. Nevertheless, the situation is not quite as simple as that, and White must be prepared to sacrifice his bishop on h6 if he is to obtain a winning position; by simply playing 1. Qg3, White would only gain a relatively small advantage, e.g. 1... g6 2. Bg5 Qc5 3. Nf6+ Bxf6 4. Bxf6, when Black can counter with 4... h6 followed by ...Kh7. Only 1. Bh6! guarantees complete success; the main reason why it is better to move the bishop rather than the queen is that in order to attack g7 the bishop has only the one move to h6, whereas the queen has a choice between c3 and g3. Thus the bishop enters the fray first, while the queen waits to see which will be better, depending on Black's reply. Thus:
zh: 轮到白方走，攻击g7的前景极佳。白马已经盯住这格，后和象也都只需一步就能对它构成威胁。一个非常有利的条件是：后可以选择从c3或g3发动攻击。不过，事情并没有这么简单；白方要取得胜势，必须准备在h6弃象。仅走1. Qg3，只能得到比较小的优势，例如1... g6 2. Bg5 Qc5 3. Nf6+ Bxf6 4. Bxf6，黑方可以用4... h6，接着...Kh7进行反击。只有1. Bh6!才能确保进攻完全成功。先动象而不先动后的主要原因在于：象要攻击g7，只有到h6这一种选择，而后可以选择c3或g3。因此，象先投入战斗，后则等待黑方应招之后，再判断该去哪里。具体如下：

text: If 1... gxh6, then 2. Qc3 f6 (if 2... Bf8, then 3. Nf6+ leads to a quick conclusion) 3. Qg3+ Bg4 (otherwise the queen mates on g7) 4. Qxg4+ Kf7 5. Qg7+ Ke6 6. Nf4+ Kd7 7. Nd5 followed by 8. Nxf6+. In this variation the queen is most effective if it goes first to c3 and then to g3.
zh: 如果1... gxh6，则2. Qc3 f6（如果2... Bf8，3. Nf6+便很快结束战斗）3. Qg3+ Bg4（否则后在g7将杀）4. Qxg4+ Kf7 5. Qg7+ Ke6 6. Nf4+ Kd7 7. Nd5，接着8. Nxf6+。在这个变化中，后先到c3，再到g3，效率最高。

text: If 1... Bf8, then White plays 2. Bxg7 Bxg7 3. Qg3 Kf8 4. Qxg7+ Ke7 5. Qg5+ Kf8 6. Rd3 or 6. Nf6.
zh: 如果1... Bf8，白方就走2. Bxg7 Bxg7 3. Qg3 Kf8 4. Qxg7+ Ke7 5. Qg5+ Kf8 6. Rd3，或6. Nf6。

text: **2. Qc3 f6 3. Nxf6+** and White wins, for after 3... Bxf6 4. Qxf6 Black has no defence against mate on g7.
zh: **2. Qc3 f6 3. Nxf6+**，白方获胜，因为3... Bxf6 4. Qxf6之后，黑方无法防住g7的将杀。

text: In order not to be unfair to Black, who tends to suffer in books such as this, here are some actual cases where White came to grief on the analogous square — g2. This position arose in the game Coria–Capablanca, Buenos Aires 1914. Black, to move, attacks g2:
zh: 在这类书中，倒霉的往往是黑方。为了不偏心，下面也给出几个实战例子，看看白方怎样在对应的g2格上遭殃。图中局面出现在1914年在布宜诺斯艾利斯的科里亚对卡帕布兰卡一局。轮到黑方走，他向g2发动攻击：
caption_zh: 科里亚（白）对卡帕布兰卡（黑），黑方行棋

text: 1... Bh3! 2. Ne3 Bxg2 3. Nf5
zh: 1... Bh3! 2. Ne3 Bxg2 3. Nf5

text: White played this in desperation; if 3. Nxg2 Qg5 4. f3, Black plays 4... Nh3+ and wins White's queen — a typical trick in positions such as this.
zh: 白方这步已经是无奈之举；如果3. Nxg2 Qg5 4. f3，黑方走4... Nh3+便能得后，这是此类局面中的典型手段。

text: This position is taken from Field–Tenner, New York 1933. It is Black's move.
zh: 这一局面来自1933年在纽约的菲尔德对滕纳一局。黑方行棋。
caption_zh: 菲尔德（白）对滕纳（黑），黑方行棋

text: The attack on g2, with its threat of mate, is carried on regardless. White resigned since he sees that 3. gxh3 is followed by 3... Nxh3#.
zh: 黑方不理会白方的应对，继续攻击g2并威胁将杀。白方看到3. gxh3之后有3... Nxh3#，于是认输。

text: ¹ It is interesting to note that White cannot save himself, even with another second move, e.g. 2. Nd3 Ne2+ 3. Kh1 Bxg2+ 4. Kxg2 Qf3+ 5. Kh3 exd3 6. Qd2 g5 or 2. Qe3 Nxg2 3. Qd2 Nf4.
zh: ¹ 值得注意的是，白方即使在第二步另选应招，也无法自救，例如2. Nd3 Ne2+ 3. Kh1 Bxg2+ 4. Kxg2 Qf3+ 5. Kh3 exd3 6. Qd2 g5，或2. Qe3 Nxg2 3. Qd2 Nf4。

text: The following position arose in the game Boleslavsky–Ufimtsev, Semi-finals USSR Championship, Omsk 1944. The Soviet master and geologist Ufimtsev, playing Black, overcame his great opponent as follows:
zh: 以下局面出现在1944年在鄂木斯克举行的苏联锦标赛半决赛中，波列斯拉夫斯基对乌菲姆采夫一局。执黑的苏联大师兼地质学家乌菲姆采夫，用以下手段击败了这位强大的对手：
caption_zh: 波列斯拉夫斯基（白）对乌菲姆采夫（黑），黑方行棋

text: After 2. Bxb6 Nxd2 White cannot play 3. Nxd2 because of the attack on g2, so he would lose either his bishop on b6 or his knight on f3.
zh: 2. Bxb6 Nxd2之后，由于g2受到攻击，白方不能走3. Nxd2，于是b6象和f3马中必有一子丢失。

text: Not 3. Bxb6 because of 3... Rxg2+ 4. Kh1 Rxh2+ 5. Nxh2 Nxf2#.
zh: 不能走3. Bxb6，因为有3... Rxg2+ 4. Kh1 Rxh2+ 5. Nxh2 Nxf2#。

text: 3... Rxg2+ 4. Nxg2 Nd2!
zh: 3... Rxg2+ 4. Nxg2 Nd2!

text: Black threatens 5... Rxg2+ 6. Kh1 Rxh2+ 7. Kg1 Rh1#. If 5. f3, then 5... Qxe3+ wins.
zh: 黑方威胁5... Rxg2+ 6. Kh1 Rxh2+ 7. Kg1 Rh1#。如果5. f3，则5... Qxe3+获胜。

text: 5. Qd5 Bxd5 6. cxd5 Qxb2 7. Bxd2 Qxa1 8. Bf3 Bxh2+ 0-1
zh: 5. Qd5 Bxd5 6. cxd5 Qxb2 7. Bxd2 Qxa1 8. Bf3 Bxh2+ 0-1

text: White has escaped being mated, but has to surrender owing to the great material losses he has suffered.
zh: 白方虽然逃过了将杀，但子力损失太大，仍不得不认输。

text: The next two games illustrate the attack on the castled king, with g2 (or g7) as the focal-point.
zh: 接下来两盘棋展示以g2（或g7）为焦点，对易位后的王发动攻击。

text:
Vygodchikov – Alekhine
Correspondence Game, 1908/9
Ruy Lopez
zh:
维戈德奇科夫—阿廖欣
1908—1909年，通信棋
西班牙开局

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Bc5
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Bc5

text: The Moller Variation, against which White can gain a slight advantage by playing 6. c3. In continuing 6. Nxe5, as he does here, White makes the defence somewhat easier for Black.
zh: 这是默勒尔变例，白方走6. c3可以取得些许优势。本局白方选择6. Nxe5，反而让黑方更容易防守。

text: 6. Nxe5 Nxe5 7. d4 Nxe4! 8. Re1 Be7 9. Rxe4 Ng6 10. Nc3?!
zh: 6. Nxe5 Nxe5 7. d4 Nxe4! 8. Re1 Be7 9. Rxe4 Ng6 10. Nc3?!

text: 10. c4 is stronger.
Instead of this weak move, correct is 12... b5! 13. Bb3 Bb7 with the better prospects for Black.
zh: 黑方不该走这一步软着，而应走12... b5! 13. Bb3 Bb7，前景更好。

text: 13. Bb3! Kh8
zh: 13. Bb3! Kh8

text: 13... fxe4 is impossible because of 14. Ne7+ Kh8 15. Nxg6+ and 16. Qh3+. Alekhine now has an inferior position.
zh: 13... fxe4行不通，因为有14. Ne7+ Kh8 15. Nxg6+，接着16. Qh3+。阿廖欣的局面现在已经处于劣势。

caption_zh: 黑方走完14... f4后的局面

text: The beginning of a bad plan. It admittedly brings White material gains but at the same time exposes him to a relentless attack on his castled position. Correct was 15. Bd2 c6 (after 15... Nh4 16. Qh5 f3 White can happily reply 17. Re4) 16. Bb4! Bxb4 17. Nxb4 d5 18. Rae1 and White has the advantage¹.
zh: 这是一个错误计划的开端。白方确实因此赢得了子力，却也让自己的王城暴露在猛烈而持续的攻击之下。正确的走法是15. Bd2 c6（15... Nh4 16. Qh5 f3之后，白方可以从容应以17. Re4）16. Bb4! Bxb4 17. Nxb4 d5 18. Rae1，白方有优势¹。

text: ¹ Vuković's line loses a piece after 17... a5 18. Nd3 a4 19. Bc4 d5, so the move actually played is probably best.
zh: ¹ 武科维奇给出的变化在17... a5 18. Nd3 a4 19. Bc4 d5之后会失子，因此实战走法很可能才是最佳选择。

text: A further mistake; 16. Nc3 would have been preferable.
zh: 又是一步错误；16. Nc3更好。

text: Now all Black's pieces come into play except the rook, and this Alekhine logically gives up, for he does not need it.
zh: 现在黑方除了车以外，所有棋子都参加了战斗。阿廖欣顺势弃掉了这辆车，因为已经不需要它了。

text: 18. Nxa8 Nh4 (D)
zh: 18. Nxa8 Nh4 (D)
caption_zh: 黑方走完18... Nh4后的局面

text: If 19. Qh5 then 19... g6 20. Qh6 Bg4 threatening both 21... Bxe2 and 21... Nf5².
zh: 如果19. Qh5，则19... g6 20. Qh6 Bg4，同时威胁21... Bxe2和21... Nf5²。

text: ² Alekhine gave 20... Nf5 followed by 21... Nxd4 in his notes. Indeed, after Vuković's 20... Bg4, White may play 21. Re5! Bxe5 22. dxe5, threatening 23. Bxf4, when Black's attack collapses.
zh: ² 阿廖欣在自己的评注中给出20... Nf5，接着21... Nxd4。事实上，按照武科维奇给出的20... Bg4，白方可以走21. Re5! Bxe5 22. dxe5，威胁23. Bxf4，黑方的进攻就瓦解了。

text: In an attempt to contain Black's attack, White gives back some of the extra material, but there is no longer any way out.
zh: 白方为遏制黑方的进攻，归还了一部分多出的子力，但已经没有出路。

text: 20... Bxe5 21. dxe5 Nxg2
zh: 20... Bxe5 21. dxe5 Nxg2

text: Naturally, Black takes on g2 with the knight and not the pawn, for he does not want to block the square g2, which is to be the focal-point of the attack.
zh: 黑方自然用马而不是兵吃g2，因为他不想堵住这个即将成为进攻焦点的格子。

text: 22. Qd4 Qd7 23. e6 Qxe6 24. Bd2 Qg6 25. Bc2
zh: 22. Qd4 Qd7 23. e6 Qxe6 24. Bd2 Qg6 25. Bc2

text: White gives up still more, but the destruction is not halted!
zh: 白方又交出更多子力，却仍挡不住攻势！

caption_zh: 白方走完28. Nb6后的局面

text: Black no longer plays for mate but instead simplifies to obtain a winning position.
zh: 黑方不再追求将杀，而是通过简化局面取得胜势。

text: 29. Rxg6 Bg2+ 30. Rxg2 fxg2+ 31. Kg1 Ne2+ 32. Kxg2 Nxd4 0-1
zh: 29. Rxg6 Bg2+ 30. Rxg2 fxg2+ 31. Kg1 Ne2+ 32. Kxg2 Nxd4 0-1

text:
Alekhine – Lasker
Zurich, 1934
Queen's Gambit Declined, Orthodox Defence
zh:
阿廖欣—拉斯克
1934年，苏黎世
拒后翼弃兵，正统防御

text: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bg5 Nbd7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. Ne4
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bg5 Nbd7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. Ne4

text: Alekhine's move; it is equally as good as 11. O-O.
zh: 阿廖欣的走法，与11. O-O同样好。

text: 12... Qb4+ 13. Qd2 Qxd2+ is sounder, with a queenless middlegame, which Capablanca drew as Black in seven games against Alekhine in their 1927 World Championship Match.
zh: 12... Qb4+ 13. Qd2 Qxd2+更稳健，进入无后中局。在1927年的世界冠军赛中，卡帕布兰卡执黑对阿廖欣时，有七盘棋在这种中局里弈和。

text: 13. O-O exd4 (D)
zh: 13. O-O exd4 (D)
caption_zh: 黑方走完13... exd4后的局面

text: This move is slightly weaker than the straightforward 14. exd4, which poses Black problems.
zh: 这步略逊于直接14. exd4，后者会给黑方带来难题。

text: 14... Qd8 15. N3xd4 Ne5 16. Bb3 Bxf5 17. Nxf5 Qb6
zh: 14... Qd8 15. N3xd4 Ne5 16. Bb3 Bxf5 17. Nxf5 Qb6

text: Unnecessarily misplacing the queen. Correct was 17... g6 18. Nd6 (or 18. Qd6 Re8) 18... Qe7, when Black can put up a good defence.
zh: 黑方没有必要把后走到这个不合适的位置。正确的是17... g6 18. Nd6（或18. Qd6 Re8）18... Qe7，黑方可以有效防守。

text: 18. Qd6 Ned7 19. Rfd1 Rad8 20. Qg3 (D)
zh: 18. Qd6 Ned7 19. Rfd1 Rad8 20. Qg3 (D)
caption_zh: 白方走完20. Qg3后的局面

text: The decisive battle for the focal-point g7 begins.
zh: 围绕g7焦点的决战开始了。

text: White threatened 22. Rd6; if 21... Qb5, then 22. Ne7+ Kg7 23. Qxb5 cxb5 24. Rc7 is in White's favour.
zh: 白方原先威胁22. Rd6；如果21... Qb5，则22. Ne7+ Kg7 23. Qxb5 cxb5 24. Rc7，白方有利。

text: A strong move, which not only prepares e5 but also clears the third rank so that White can bring a rook into the attack.
zh: 这是一步强棋，不仅准备冲起e5，还腾出了第三横线，使白方能把车调来参加进攻。

caption_zh: 黑方走完23... Ng8后的局面

text: This hastens the end, but 23... Ne8 was just as inadequate in view of 24. Nf5+ followed by 25. Qe7¹.
zh: 这步加速了败局，但23... Ne8同样不够，因为白方有24. Nf5+，接着25. Qe7¹。

text: ¹ 24. Nxb7, winning a piece, is even more convincing.
zh: ¹ 24. Nxb7得子，更有说服力。

text: If 24... h6, there follows the other variation of Alekhine's elegant combination: 25. Nf5+ Kh7 26. Nxh6 f6 (or 26... Nxh6 27. Rh3) 27. Nf5! fxg5 28. Rh3+ mating.
zh: 如果24... h6，便出现阿廖欣这个精妙组合的另一变化：25. Nf5+ Kh7 26. Nxh6 f6（或26... Nxh6 27. Rh3）27. Nf5! fxg5 28. Rh3+，将杀。

text: Since 26... hxg6 is answered by 27. Rh3+ and mate. A pointed end to a game which contained some typical manoeuvres in the struggle by the queen and knight for the focal-point g7.
zh: 因为26... hxg6会遭到27. Rh3+并将杀。这盘棋以一个漂亮的点睛之笔收尾，展示了后与马争夺g7焦点时的若干典型调动。

text: Further examples of play against the focal-point g7 are contained in the chapter on fianchettoed positions.
zh: 关于侧翼出象局面的章节，还会给出更多攻击g7焦点的例子。

text: The focal-point h7
zh: h7焦点

text: While the attacker cannot easily target g7, the square h7 is often exposed to danger even in the opening stages of a game, although attacks based on h7 as a focal-point are generally not so dangerous as those aimed at g7. This important point has already been noted, together with the reason for it, i.e. the fact that the king can escape from g8 to f8, whereas to avoid the threat of the queen on g7 the king has to travel further (to e8 or e7). Because of this, the main task involved in attacks on the focal-point g7 is the 'clearing' of that square, while the possible escape of the king is a minor worry. In attacks on h7 the 'clearing' is usually the easier task, while the attacker's main preoccupation is to stop the king escaping; this means essentially that he should have a new focal-point in view, if the attack is to be successful. In other words, the possible escape of the king turns the primary focal-point h7 into a secondary one, so that a new, real focal-point becomes necessary. It is worth keeping this important fact in mind, since in practice the majority of possible attacks on h7 founder precisely on the king's use of the simple defensive expedient of running away.
zh: 进攻方不容易把矛头对准g7，但h7格往往在开局阶段就会受到威胁。尽管如此，以h7为焦点的攻击通常没有针对g7的攻击那么危险。前面已经指出这一重要区别及其原因：王可以从g8逃到f8，而要躲开g7后的威胁，就必须逃得更远，到e8或e7。因此，攻击g7焦点时，主要任务是“清除”这格上的障碍，王可能逃走则是次要顾虑。攻击h7时，“清除”往往更容易，进攻方最需要考虑的反而是阻止王逃走；也就是说，要使进攻成功，就必须预先瞄准一个新的焦点。换言之，王可能逃走，使原先的h7焦点退居次要位置，进攻方因而需要一个新的、真正起决定作用的焦点。值得牢记这一点，因为实战中许多本来可能成立的h7攻击，恰恰是由于王采用了逃跑这一简单防守手段而失败。

text: These factors, which apply to most attacks on h7, are well illustrated by the following example.
zh: 下例很好地说明了这些适用于大多数h7攻击的因素。

text: White, to move, begins with **1. Qb1!**. Black's queen has to guard the square e8, and so has only two replies:
zh: 白方行棋，以**1. Qb1!**开始进攻。黑后必须保护e8格，因此只有两种应招：

text: 1) **1... Qd7 2. Re7!** (after 2. Rxe8+? Qxe8 3. Qh7+ Kf8 White's attack comes to a dead end, since the black king has e7 to escape to) **2... Qxe7** (2... Rxe7 has the same effect, while if 2... Qd8, then 3. Qh7+ followed by 4. Rxf7#) **3. Qh7+ Kf8 4. Qh8#**.
zh: 1）**1... Qd7 2. Re7!**（2. Rxe8+? Qxe8 3. Qh7+ Kf8之后，黑王可以逃到e7，白方的进攻便走到了尽头）**2... Qxe7**（2... Rxe7的效果相同；如果2... Qd8，则3. Qh7+，接着4. Rxf7#）**3. Qh7+ Kf8 4. Qh8#**。

text: 2) **1... Qc6 2. d5 Qc8 3. Rxe8+** (this is all right now, but 3. Re7? would not do because of 3... Bxg5) **3... Qxe8 4. Qh7+ Kf8 5. d6**, and Black cannot avoid mate next move by **6. Qh8#**.
zh: 2）**1... Qc6 2. d5 Qc8 3. Rxe8+**（现在这样走就可以了；反倒是3. Re7?不行，因为有3... Bxg5）**3... Qxe8 4. Qh7+ Kf8 5. d6**，黑方无法避免下一步**6. Qh8#**。

text: White's combination, then, has two variations, and the point of each is to deprive Black's king of an escape to e7, either by blocking it or playing d6. The square h7 appears here as a secondary focal-point, while the crucial factor in the combination is the mate when the king reaches f8.
zh: 白方的组合有两个变化，关键都是不让黑王逃到e7：或者把e7堵住，或者冲起d6控制这格。h7在这里是次要焦点，组合的决定性环节，是在黑王逃到f8后将杀。

text: There is in fact such an abundance of attacks against the castled king with a real or secondary focal-point at h7, and they differ so widely, that an attempt to systematize them would take us too far afield; let us be content with a few general examples, and then deal in more detail with 'the classic bishop sacrifice on h7', which in practice is the most important kind of attack on the focal-point h7.
zh: 以h7为主要或次要焦点的王城攻击实在太多，而且差别很大；若要把它们系统分类，就会偏离本书的讨论范围。因此，我们只看几个一般性的例子，然后再详细讨论“h7经典弃象”，这是实战中针对h7焦点最重要的攻击方式。

text: This position arose in Szabo–Kotov, Groningen 1946. It is White's move, and he effects the 'clearing' of the focal-point h7 by eliminating the knight on f6:
zh: 这一局面出现在1946年在格罗宁根的萨博对科托夫一局。白方行棋，他通过消灭f6马，完成对h7焦点的“清除”：
caption_zh: 萨博（白）对科托夫（黑），白方行棋

text: 1. Nd5! exd5 2. Bxf6 Bf5
zh: 1. Nd5! exd5 2. Bxf6 Bf5

text: The only reply, though an inadequate one.
zh: 唯一的应招，但仍不足以应付进攻。

text: 3. Qxf5 g6
zh: 3. Qxf5 g6

text: White now continued with 4. Qxg6+ fxg6 5. Bxd5+ Rf7 6. Bxe7 and won on the basis of his material advantage, but 4. Bxe7 gxf5 5. Bxf8 would have been even clearer.
zh: 白方接着走4. Qxg6+ fxg6 5. Bxd5+ Rf7 6. Bxe7，凭借子力优势获胜。不过，4. Bxe7 gxf5 5. Bxf8更为清楚。

text: Here we have a straightforward example of the creation of a mating position by directing the queen and a pawn against the focal-point h7, followed by a typical new mate after the black king has escaped.
zh: 下图是一个简单明了的例子：后与兵共同指向h7焦点，构成将杀局面；黑王逃走后，又会出现一个典型的新将杀。

text: 1. Bxh7+ Kxh7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. g6 Re8 4. Qh7+ Kf8 5. Qh8+ Ke7 6. Qxg7#.
zh: 1. Bxh7+ Kxh7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. g6 Re8 4. Qh7+ Kf8 5. Qh8+ Ke7 6. Qxg7#.

text: In this position Black aims to drive White's rook from f4 and then proceed with ...g3, creating a threat against h2. He plays:
zh: 下图中，黑方想把白车赶离f4，接着冲起g3，对h2构成威胁。他这样走：

text: If 2. d4 Bxf4 3. Bxf4, Black continues 3... g3 4. Qf3 Qh2+ 5. Kf1 Qh1+ 6. Ke2 Nf6 7. Qxg3 Bg4+ 8. Ke3 Qc1+ 9. Kd3 Qf1+ 10. Kc2 Qxc4 and wins.
zh: 如果2. d4 Bxf4 3. Bxf4，黑方接着走3... g3 4. Qf3 Qh2+ 5. Kf1 Qh1+ 6. Ke2 Nf6 7. Qxg3 Bg4+ 8. Ke3 Qc1+ 9. Kd3 Qf1+ 10. Kc2 Qxc4，获胜。

text: If 2. Qf3 Bxf4 3. Qxf4 Qe1+ 4. Kh2 (both 4. Bf1 Rh7 and 4. Qf1 Qxf1+ 5. Kxf1 Rh7 are in Black's favour) 4... Nf6! 5. Nxh8, Black wins by 5... g3+ 6. Qxg3 Ng4+.
zh: 如果2. Qf3 Bxf4 3. Qxf4 Qe1+ 4. Kh2（4. Bf1 Rh7和4. Qf1 Qxf1+ 5. Kxf1 Rh7都对黑方有利）4... Nf6! 5. Nxh8，黑方用5... g3+ 6. Qxg3 Ng4+获胜。

text: If 3. Rf1, Black plays 3... O-O-O and then ...g3, forcing mate. At once 3... g3 would not be good because of 4. Bf7+ and 5. Qh5.
zh: 如果3. Rf1，黑方走3... O-O-O，接着...g3，便能强制将杀。立即3... g3则不好，因为有4. Bf7+，接着5. Qh5。

text: This move is now playable; indeed, it is obligatory, since after 3... O-O-O 4. d3 g3 Black is a tempo behind with his attack; White then has the following defence, a characteristic one in such positions: 5. Be3 Qh2+ 6. Kf1 Qh1+ 7. Bg1, and Black's attack has come to nothing.
zh: 现在这步可以走了，而且非走不可；因为3... O-O-O 4. d3 g3之后，黑方的进攻就慢了一个先手。白方于是可以采用此类局面中很典型的防守：5. Be3 Qh2+ 6. Kf1 Qh1+ 7. Bg1，黑方的进攻便落空了。

text: 4. Qf3 Bg4! (D)
zh: 4. Qf3 Bg4! (D)

text: A typical method of preparing the mating net; one should not check if this only simplifies the opponent's defence. It should be noted that checking at h2 and then h1 loses a tempo. Black's aim is to oblige the white king to move to f1 of its own free will, and then give check with the queen directly at h1, without stopping at h2.
zh: 这是编织杀网的典型方法：如果将军只会让对方更容易防守，就不该将军。注意，先在h2、再在h1将军，会损失一个先手。黑方的目标是迫使白王自行走到f1，然后后直接到h1将军，不在h2停留。

text: 5. Rf8+ Kd7 6. Rf7+
zh: 5. Rf8+ Kd7 6. Rf7+

text: If 6. Qf7+, then 6... Nge7, while 6. Be6+ is answered by 6... Bxe6! 7. Rxa8 Nf6! 8. Rxh8 Qh2+ 9. Kf1 Qh1+ 10. Ke2 Bg4 and wins. Lastly, 6. Qd3+ is simply met by 6... Nd4.
zh: 如果6. Qf7+，则6... Nge7；如果6. Be6+，则6... Bxe6! 7. Rxa8 Nf6! 8. Rxh8 Qh2+ 9. Kf1 Qh1+ 10. Ke2 Bg4，黑方获胜。至于6. Qd3+，简单应以6... Nd4即可。

text: **6... Nge7 7. Qe3 Raf8** and Black wins easily, for example after 8. Kf1 Rxf7+ 9. Bxf7 Rf8.
zh: **6... Nge7 7. Qe3 Raf8**，黑方轻松获胜，例如8. Kf1 Rxf7+ 9. Bxf7 Rf8。

text: For our final example in this section let us examine the main line of the Moller Attack in the Giuoco Piano. In this White's attack, involving the sacrifice of a knight on h7, is so strong — or weak — that the game ends in a draw.
zh: 本节最后一个例子，我们来看意大利开局中默勒尔进攻的主线。白方在h7弃马发动的进攻，不强不弱，恰好足以使对局以和棋告终。

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Nc3 Nxe4 8. O-O Bxc3 9. d5
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Nc3 Nxe4 8. O-O Bxc3 9. d5

text: Moller's strengthening of the attack; 9. bxc3 used to be played, whereupon Black obtains the advantage by 9... d5.
zh: 默勒尔用这步加强进攻；过去通常走9. bxc3，黑方可用9... d5取得优势。

text: The best reply.
zh: 最佳应招。

text: 10. Re1 Ne7 11. Rxe4 d6
zh: 10. Re1 Ne7 11. Rxe4 d6

text: If 11... O-O, then 12. d6 is reckoned to give White good prospects.
zh: 如果11... O-O，一般认为12. d6会给白方带来良好前景。

text: 12. Bg5 Bxg5 13. Nxg5 O-O¹ 14. Nxh7 Kxh7 15. Qh5+ Kg8 16. Rh4 f5 (D)
zh: 12. Bg5 Bxg5 13. Nxg5 O-O¹ 14. Nxh7 Kxh7 15. Qh5+ Kg8 16. Rh4 f5 (D)
caption_zh: 黑方走完16... f5后的局面

text: Instead of 16... f5 Bogoljubow suggested and experimented with 16... f6, which is weaker.
zh: 波戈留波夫曾建议并试验过以16... f6代替16... f5，但前者较弱。

text: ¹ Current theory reckons 13... h6 to be best, when White is struggling for equality.
zh: ¹ 编者写作时的理论认为13... h6最佳，白方要为争取均势而努力。

text: In the position after 16... f5, White must try to justify the sacrifice of the knight. Admittedly, he controls the square h7, but, at the same time, he cannot prevent the black king from escaping via f7 when it is checked. If the game is continued correctly, White can only obtain perpetual check, not mate. Both 17. Qh7+ (variation A) and 17. Rh3 (B) lead to a draw, while the rest end in a win for Black. These other, poorer, continuations are given under (C) and (D).
zh: 16... f5之后，白方必须设法证明弃马成立。他确实控制了h7格，但与此同时，又无法阻止黑王在受到将军后经f7逃走。双方走法正确时，白方只能取得长将，不能将杀。17. Qh7+（变化A）和17. Rh3（变化B）都能弈和，其余走法则以黑方获胜告终。这些较差的后续手段列在变化C和D中。

text: This is the oldest method, tried out in innumerable games and ending in a draw.
zh: 这是最早的办法，在无数对局中得到过检验，结局为和棋。

text: 18. Re1 is not good because of 18... Ng6 19. Rh6 Qg5, etc.
zh: 18. Re1不好，因为有18... Ng6 19. Rh6 Qg5等。

caption_zh: 白方走完19. Re1后的局面

text: Maroczy, and later Bogoljubow, tried to find a win for Black at this point with 19... Kf8 but further analyses have shown that White has a draw by 20. Rh3! Bd7 (if 20... f4 then 21. Rh4 is in White's favour) 21. Rhe3 Nc8 22. Bd3 g6 (if 22... Nb6, White wins by 23. Bxf5 Nxd5 24. Bxd7! Nxe3 — or 24... Qxd7 25. Rf3+ — 25. Be6 Ke7 26. Rxe3) 23. h4 Rg7 24. Qh8+ Rg8 25. Qh7, repeating moves. Possibly one could also play for a win here with 25. Qh6+ Kf7 26. Re6.
zh: 马洛契，以及后来的波戈留波夫，都曾试图用19... Kf8为黑方寻找赢棋。但进一步分析表明，白方可以用20. Rh3! Bd7（如果20... f4，21. Rh4对白方有利）21. Rhe3 Nc8 22. Bd3 g6（如果22... Nb6，白方以23. Bxf5 Nxd5 24. Bxd7! Nxe3——或24... Qxd7 25. Rf3+——25. Be6 Ke7 26. Rxe3获胜）23. h4 Rg7 24. Qh8+ Rg8 25. Qh7，通过重复局面弈和。这里也许还能用25. Qh6+ Kf7 26. Re6争取赢棋。

text: 20. Be2 is weaker, since after 20... Ke8 Black's king escapes to d8.
zh: 20. Be2较弱，因为20... Ke8之后，黑王可以逃到d8。

text: 20... c6? is bad because of 21. dxc6 while if 20... a6?, then 21. Ree6 axb5 22. Rhf6+ with advantage to White.
zh: 20... c6?不好，因为有21. dxc6；如果20... a6?，则21. Ree6 axb5 22. Rhf6+，白方占优。

text: **21. Qxh8 gxh6 22. Qh7+ Kf6 23. Rxe7! Qxe7 24. Qxh6+**, and White forces perpetual check.
zh: **21. Qxh8 gxh6 22. Qh7+ Kf6 23. Rxe7! Qxe7 24. Qxh6+**，白方强制长将。

text: White's other sound continuation, discovered by Keres.
zh: 白方另一种可靠的后续手段，由凯列斯发现。

text: According to Keres, all other moves give White the advantage.
zh: 按照凯列斯的分析，其他走法都会让白方占优。

text: **18. g4 fxg3 19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. Qh5+ Kg8 21. Qh7+** with perpetual check.

Against 20... g6 Keres gives 21. Qh7+ Ke8 22. Rxg3 and White stands better, but Black can improve by 21... Kf6 22. Qh4+ Kf7 and draws. Black would probably not be able to venture on 22... g5 23. Qh6+ Ng6 24. Rh5 gxf2+ 25. Kxf2 since if 25... Ke5+ White can boldly play 26. Ke3.
zh: 针对20... g6，凯列斯给出21. Qh7+ Ke8 22. Rxg3，白方较好；但黑方可以改进为21... Kf6 22. Qh4+ Kf7，弈和。黑方大概不能冒险走22... g5 23. Qh6+ Ng6 24. Rh5 gxf2+ 25. Kxf2，因为如果25... Ke5+，白方可以大胆地走26. Ke3。

text: Now we examine White's weaker continuations.
zh: 现在来看白方较弱的后续手段。

text: 18. Qh8+ Kf7 19. Bh5+ is not sufficient for a draw on account of 19... Ng6.
zh: 18. Qh8+ Kf7 19. Bh5+不足以弈和，因为有19... Ng6。

text: Or 19. Qh8+ Ng8!.
**19... Bd7 20. Re6 Ng8!** and White's attack is driven back¹.
zh: **19... Bd7 20. Re6 Ng8!**，白方的进攻被击退¹。

text: ¹ At the end of this line 21. Qxf5+ Nf6 22. Bxd7 Qxd7 23. Rxf6+ wins for White, so Black must search for an improvement earlier. 17... Ng6 18. Qh7+ Kf7 19. Rh6 Nf4 20. Bh5+ Nxh5 21. Qg6+ Kg8 22. Qxh5 gxh6 23. Qg6+ with a draw may well be Black's best, so 17. Be2 probably doesn't deserve a question mark.
zh: ¹ 在这条变化的最后，白方有21. Qxf5+ Nf6 22. Bxd7 Qxd7 23. Rxf6+获胜，因此黑方必须在更早的地方寻找改进。17... Ng6 18. Qh7+ Kf7 19. Rh6 Nf4 20. Bh5+ Nxh5 21. Qg6+ Kg8 22. Qxh5 gxh6 23. Qg6+，以和棋告终，很可能才是黑方的最佳选择。因此，17. Be2大概不该标问号。

caption_zh: 白方走完18. Rh3后的局面

text: 18... f4 is weaker because of 19. Re6 and so is 18... Nf4?, e.g. 19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. Rhe3 Ng6 21. Qh5 followed by Re7+, etc².
zh: 18... f4较弱，因为有19. Re6；18... Nf4?也较弱，例如19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. Rhe3 Ng6 21. Qh5，接着Re7+等²。

text: ² However 21... Qf6 seems to defend, e.g. 22. Re7+ Kg8 or 22. Re6 Bxe6 23. Rxe6 Qxb2 24. Qxg6+ Kg8. Therefore White should prefer 21. Rg3! Qf6 22. Re6! Bxe6 23. dxe6+ Ke8 24. Rxg6 with advantage.
zh: ² 不过，21... Qf6似乎能够守住，例如22. Re7+ Kg8，或22. Re6 Bxe6 23. Rxe6 Qxb2 24. Qxg6+ Kg8。因此，白方应选择21. Rg3! Qf6 22. Re6! Bxe6 23. dxe6+ Ke8 24. Rxg6，取得优势。

text: This is relatively the best way out for White. 19. Re6 Bxe6 20. Qh7+ Kf8 21. dxe6 d5 is inadequate for White, and he loses.
zh: 这是白方相对最好的出路。19. Re6 Bxe6 20. Qh7+ Kf8 21. dxe6 d5对白方不够，白方会输。

text: Keres played 19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. Re6 in several correspondence games and he gives this continuation in his handbook Theorie der Schacheröffnungen. Nevertheless, Black can then win by 20... Nf8 21. Qh5+ g6, etc. This simple continuation was, strangely enough, not noticed by Keres's 'correspondence customers', and Euwe also fails to record it in his opening works, giving instead a draw by 20... Bxe6? 21. dxe6+ Rxe6 22. Bxe6+ Kxe6 23. Qxg6+ Qf6 24. Re3+, etc.
zh: 凯列斯在几盘通信棋中走过19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. Re6，并把这一后续手段收入他的开局谱《国际象棋开局理论》。然而，黑方接着20... Nf8 21. Qh5+ g6等就能获胜。奇怪的是，凯列斯的那些“通信棋客户”竟都没有发现这条简单变化。尤伟在自己的开局著作中也没有记载它，而是给出20... Bxe6? 21. dxe6+ Rxe6 22. Bxe6+ Kxe6 23. Qxg6+ Qf6 24. Re3+等，并判为和棋。

text: The only reply. 19... Kf7? 20. Re6! is in White's favour, for he wins back his sacrificed piece and keeps up his attack.
zh: 唯一的应招。19... Kf7? 20. Re6!对白方有利，因为他能吃回弃掉的棋子，同时保持进攻。

text: Neither 20. Rxe5 dxe5 21. d6+ Be6 nor 20. Qg5 Qf8 leads anywhere.
zh: 无论20. Rxe5 dxe5 21. d6+ Be6，还是20. Qg5 Qf8，都无济于事。

text: White's attack has come to a halt and Black has an adequate defence, for example if 22. Re7, then 22... Nh6 followed by 23... Rf7.
zh: 白方的进攻停滞了，黑方可以有效防守。例如22. Re7，可应以22... Nh6，接着23... Rf7。

text: The reader will find further examples concerning the focal-point h7 in the next chapter, which deals with the classic bishop sacrifice. These examples provide a typical illustration of the part played by the square h7 as a mating and secondary focal-point.
zh: 下一章讨论经典弃象，读者会在那里看到更多关于h7焦点的例子。它们典型地展示了h7格作为将杀焦点或次要焦点所起的作用。

text: The auxiliary focal-point f7
zh: 辅助焦点f7

text: Mention has already been made of the vulnerability of the square f7 before castling, and now we shall examine the part played by an assault on that square after the king has castled. First of all, it should be remarked that the square f7 is only in exceptional cases the focal-point in the true sense, i.e. the square from which mate is effected. However, it is very often an auxiliary focal-point, which is attacked either in order to drive the king away from g8 or, by means of a sacrifice, to draw the king on to the actual square itself.
zh: 前面已经讨论过易位之前f7格的脆弱性，现在来看王易位之后，攻击这格有什么作用。首先应指出，f7只有在特殊情况下才是真正的将杀焦点，也就是进攻方从这里实施将杀的格子。不过，它经常是辅助焦点：攻击f7，或者是为了把王赶离g8，或者是通过弃子把王引到f7本身。

text: The following position from the game Tylor–Koltanowski, Hastings 1930 arose after the moves **1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 d6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. e4 e5 5. Bc4 Be7 6. O-O O-O 7. Qe2 exd4 8. Nxd4 Re8** (D).
zh: 下图来自1930年在黑斯廷斯的泰勒对科尔塔诺夫斯基一局，走法是**1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 d6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. e4 e5 5. Bc4 Be7 6. O-O O-O 7. Qe2 exd4 8. Nxd4 Re8**（见图）。
caption_zh: 黑方走完8... Re8后的局面

text: White, by attacking f7, drew Black's king out from the safety of its castled position.
zh: 白方通过攻击f7，把黑王从安全的王城中引了出来。

text: 9. Bxf7+! Kxf7 10. Ne6
zh: 9. Bxf7+! Kxf7 10. Ne6

text: Making use of the familiar feature of the hemmed-in queen.
zh: 利用后被困住这一熟悉的局面特点。

text: The king cannot advance to e5 because of 13. Qf4# nor to f5 because of 13. Qd3+ with a mating attack, while if 12... Kd6, there follows 13. Nb5+ Ke5 14. Re1+ Kf5 15. Qd3+ Kg4 16. Qh3#.
zh: 王不能走到e5，因为有13. Qf4#；也不能到f5，因为13. Qd3+会发动杀王攻击。如果12... Kd6，则13. Nb5+ Ke5 14. Re1+ Kf5 15. Qd3+ Kg4 16. Qh3#。

text: After 13... Kf8 the king has returned to its shelter, but now the trouble over the hemmed-in queen reappears: 14. dxc7 and Black loses, since after 14... Nb6 15. cxd8=Q Nxc4 16. Qd4 the old white queen dies but a new one comes to life.
zh: 13... Kf8之后，王虽回到了庇护所，但后被困住的问题又出现了：14. dxc7，黑方败势，因为14... Nb6 15. cxd8=Q Nxc4 16. Qd4之后，白方旧后虽被吃掉，新后却诞生了。

text: Black therefore played **13... Nd5**, but after **14. dxe7 Rxe7 15. Nxd5** his position was hopeless.
zh: 因此黑方走了**13... Nd5**，但**14. dxe7 Rxe7 15. Nxd5**之后，他的局面已经无望。

text: The following position from the game Burn–E. Cohn, Breslau 1912 illustrates a faulty attack on f7. It was White's move and he played:
zh: 下图来自1912年在布雷斯劳的伯恩对E.科恩一局，展示了一次不正确的f7攻击。轮到白方走，他选择：
caption_zh: 伯恩（白）对E.科恩（黑），白方行棋

text: Malicious old men said that this was the only sacrifice ever risked by the cautious master Burn in his whole chess career. To this observation one might add, 'and even then it wasn't correct', as will shortly be seen.
zh: 有些爱挖苦人的老棋手说，谨慎的伯恩大师整个棋坛生涯中，只有这一次冒险弃子。对此还可以补上一句：“而且这唯一一次还不成立。”我们马上就会看到。

text: This presents White with a tempo, which is decisive. After the correct 2... Kf8! one cannot see how White's attack can succeed, for example 3. Bxf6 Bxf6 4. Qxh7 Rac8! 5. d5 Ng5 6. Qh8+ Ke7, and Black can defend himself satisfactorily.
zh: 这步白送白方一个先手，结果是决定性的。如果正确地走2... Kf8!，就看不出白方的进攻如何能够成功，例如3. Bxf6 Bxf6 4. Qxh7 Rac8! 5. d5 Ng5 6. Qh8+ Ke7，黑方可以满意地守住。

text: 3. Bxf6 Bxf6 4. Qxh7+ Kf8 5. d5
zh: 3. Bxf6 Bxf6 4. Qxh7+ Kf8 5. d5

text: Black now loses, since if he moves his knight, White plays 6. Rxf6+.
zh: 黑方现在败势，因为如果动马，白方就走6. Rxf6+。

text: **5... Qe5 6. dxe6 Qxe3+ 7. Kh1 Qxe6 8. Bg6 1-0**, for at the very least Black loses the exchange, e.g. after 8... Qg8. The alternatives 8... Rec8 9. Rde1, 8... Re7 9. Rde1! Qg8 10. Rxf6+ gxf6 11. Qxe7# and 8... Qc6 9. Qh8+ Ke7 10. Rfe1+ are even worse for Black.
zh: **5... Qe5 6. dxe6 Qxe3+ 7. Kh1 Qxe6 8. Bg6 1-0**，黑方至少要丢掉半子，例如8... Qg8。其他选择对白方更有利：8... Rec8 9. Rde1；8... Re7 9. Rde1! Qg8 10. Rxf6+ gxf6 11. Qxe7#；以及8... Qc6 9. Qh8+ Ke7 10. Rfe1+。

text: This position arose in the game Capablanca–R. Illa, Buenos Aires 1911. White's combination contains a thrust against the focal-point f7 as a preparation for the decisive action based on the real focal-point at h7.
zh: 下图出现在1911年在布宜诺斯艾利斯的卡帕布兰卡对R.伊利亚一局。白方的组合先对f7焦点发起攻击，为针对真正焦点h7的决定性行动作准备。
caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡（白）对R.伊利亚（黑），白方行棋

text: 1. Bxf6!
zh: 1. Bxf6!

text: Interesting, though inadequate, is the alternative possibility 1. Nxf6+? gxf6 2. Qh5 fxg5 3. Qh6 d4! 4. Bxd4 e5 5. Bxe5 f6 6. Bxg6 Qd7, and White loses a piece without getting enough in return¹.
zh: 另一种有趣但不够充分的选择是1. Nxf6+? gxf6 2. Qh5 fxg5 3. Qh6 d4! 4. Bxd4 e5 5. Bxe5 f6 6. Bxg6 Qd7，白方失子却得不到足够补偿¹。

text: ¹ In fact this line is also winning for White, since at the end White can continue 7. Bxf6 Rxf6 (7... hxg6 8. Qxg6+) 8. Bxh7+ Kf7 9. Bg8+ Kxg8 10. Qxf6 with the decisive material advantage of rook + four pawns v two bishops.
zh: ¹ 事实上，这条变化对白方同样是赢棋，因为最后白方可以接着走7. Bxf6 Rxf6（7... hxg6 8. Qxg6+）8. Bxh7+ Kf7 9. Bg8+ Kxg8 10. Qxf6，以车加四兵对双象，取得决定性的子力优势。

text: 1... gxf6 2. Nh6+ Kg7 3. Nhxf7
zh: 1... gxf6 2. Nh6+ Kg7 3. Nhxf7

text: Gaining an important tempo by the attack on the e-pawn.
zh: 攻击e兵，赢得重要的一个先手。

text: The capture on f7 has helped to weaken the b1–h7 diagonal, on which lies the real focal-point at h7.
zh: 吃掉f7兵，削弱了b1—h7斜线，而真正的焦点h7就在这条斜线上。

text: If 5... Kxf7, then 6. Qxh7+ Kf6 7. Bxg6 Qxg6 8. fxg5+ Ke5 (or 8... Kxg5 9. h4+!) 9. Qc7+ Ke4 10. Rxf8 and White wins.
zh: 如果5... Kxf7，则6. Qxh7+ Kf6 7. Bxg6 Qxg6 8. fxg5+ Ke5（或8... Kxg5 9. h4+!）9. Qc7+ Ke4 10. Rxf8，白方获胜。

text: Black presumably saw 6... Qe7 7. Bxg6 hxg6 8. Qxg6+ Qg7 9. Qxe6+ Kh8 10. Rf3, and decided to abandon resistance².
zh: 黑方大概看到了6... Qe7 7. Bxg6 hxg6 8. Qxg6+ Qg7 9. Qxe6+ Kh8 10. Rf3，于是决定放弃抵抗²。

text: ² Vuković overlooks the mate in two by 10... Qa1+, but of course White had several genuine winning lines, e.g. 10. Qh3+ Kg8 11. Ne6.
zh: ² 武科维奇漏算了10... Qa1+的两步杀。不过白方当然有几条真正的赢棋变化，例如10. Qh3+ Kg8 11. Ne6。

text: Black might have tried to continue with 6... Rf7 7. Bxg6 hxg6 8. Qxg6+ Kf8 9. Nxe6+ Ke7, admittedly without any real prospects of survival, e.g. 10. Rc1! Bd6 11. Ng5, etc.
zh: 黑方也许可以试着继续6... Rf7 7. Bxg6 hxg6 8. Qxg6+ Kf8 9. Nxe6+ Ke7，但确实没有什么真正的求生希望，例如10. Rc1! Bd6 11. Ng5等。

text: This position occurred in the game Najdorf–Ivkov from the last round of the tournament at Mar del Plata 1955. Black, to move, correctly decided to sacrifice his knight on f2, obtaining two pawns and a powerful attack against the exposed white king:
zh: 下图出现在1955年马德普拉塔锦标赛最后一轮的纳伊多夫对伊夫科夫一局。黑方行棋，正确地决定在f2弃马，得到两兵，并对暴露的白王发动强大攻势：
caption_zh: 纳伊多夫（白）对伊夫科夫（黑），黑方行棋

text: 16... Nxf2! 17. Kxf2 Rxe4 18. Bb2 Nc5 19. Kg1!
zh: 16... Nxf2! 17. Kxf2 Rxe4 18. Bb2 Nc5 19. Kg1!

text: White finds the best defence and withdraws his king to h1. If White had tried to retain his material advantage with 19. Kf3?, the answer would have been 19... Ne6 20. Nc2 Ng5+ 21. Kg3 Bxb2 22. Rxb2 Qc5! with a decisive attack.
zh: 白方找到了最佳防守，把王撤回h1。如果白方想用19. Kf3?保住子力优势，黑方就会应以19... Ne6 20. Nc2 Ng5+ 21. Kg3 Bxb2 22. Rxb2 Qc5!，取得决定性攻势。

text: 19... Ne6 20. Kh1 Nxd4 21. Nxd4 Rxd4!
zh: 19... Ne6 20. Kh1 Nxd4 21. Nxd4 Rxd4!

text: Not 21... Rxe1? 22. Qxe1 Bxd4 because of 23. Qe8+ Kg7 24. Qe3! c5 25. Qe7+ Kg8 26. Bxd4 cxd4 27. c5 followed by 28. Bc4+ and White wins.
zh: 不能走21... Rxe1? 22. Qxe1 Bxd4，因为有23. Qe8+ Kg7 24. Qe3! c5 25. Qe7+ Kg8 26. Bxd4 cxd4 27. c5，接着28. Bc4+，白方获胜。

text: 22. Bxd4 Qxd4 23. Qxd4 Bxd4
zh: 22. Bxd4 Qxd4 23. Qxd4 Bxd4

text: Black has re-established the material balance and is rather the better placed; after a few more moves he settled for a draw, since that was all he needed for first place.
zh: 黑方恢复了子力平衡，位置还稍好一些。再走几步后，他接受了和棋，因为和棋就足以确保第一名。

text:
Janowski and Soldatenkov – Lasker and Taubenhaus
Consultation Game, Paris, 1909
Danish Gambit
zh:
雅诺夫斯基与索尔达坚科夫—拉斯克与陶本豪斯
1909年，巴黎，商议对局
丹麦弃兵

text: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. c3 dxc3 4. Bc4 cxb2 5. Bxb2 Nf6?!
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. c3 dxc3 4. Bc4 cxb2 5. Bxb2 Nf6?!

text: Better is 5... d5 6. Bxd5 Nf6 and if 7. Bxf7+ then 7... Kxf7 8. Qxd8 Bb4+, etc.
zh: 更好的是5... d5 6. Bxd5 Nf6；如果7. Bxf7+，则7... Kxf7 8. Qxd8 Bb4+等。

text: 6. e5 Bb4+ 7. Nc3 Qe7 8. Ne2 Ne4? (D)
zh: 6. e5 Bb4+ 7. Nc3 Qe7 8. Ne2 Ne4? (D)
caption_zh: 黑方走完8... Ne4后的局面

text: This leads to the exchange of the only two minor pieces Black has developed, which inevitably adds to White's advantage in development. 8... Ng4 was worth considering, and even 8... Qxe5 would have been better than the move played.
zh: 这会让黑方仅有的两个已出轻子被兑换掉，必然进一步扩大白方的出子优势。8... Ng4值得考虑；即使8... Qxe5，也比实战这步好。

text: 9. O-O Nxc3 10. Bxc3 Bxc3 11. Nxc3 O-O 12. Nd5! Qxe5
zh: 9. O-O Nxc3 10. Bxc3 Bxc3 11. Nxc3 O-O 12. Nd5! Qxe5

text: Black would also be in difficulties after 12... Qd8 13. Qh5 d6 14. f4 but there would at least be a hope of recovery then, whereas the course actually taken holds no prospects whatever.
zh: 12... Qd8 13. Qh5 d6 14. f4之后，黑方也有困难，但至少还有挽回的希望；实战选择的道路则毫无前景。

text: 13. Re1 Qd6 14. Qh5 c6
zh: 13. Re1 Qd6 14. Qh5 c6

text: White threatened 15. Nxc7 Qxc7 16. Qxf7+ Rxf7 17. Re8#. Both 14... h6 15. Rad1! and 14... Nc6 15. Re4! were bad for Black, while if 14... g6, then 15. Qh6 Nc6 16. Re4 with an irresistible attack.
zh: 白方威胁15. Nxc7 Qxc7 16. Qxf7+ Rxf7 17. Re8#。14... h6 15. Rad1!和14... Nc6 15. Re4!都对黑方不利；如果14... g6，则15. Qh6 Nc6 16. Re4，攻势不可阻挡。

text: 15... Qxc7 provokes a catastrophe on the focal-point f7, i.e. 16. Qxf7+ and 17. Re8#.
zh: 15... Qxc7会在f7焦点引发灾难，即16. Qxf7+，接着17. Re8#。

text: 16. Qh6 Qxc7 (D)
zh: 16. Qh6 Qxc7 (D)
caption_zh: 黑方走完16... Qxc7后的局面

text: The assault on f7 is now carried out as effectively by the bishop as it was by the queen in the variation above.
zh: 现在由象来攻击f7，与上面变化中由后来攻击的效果一样好。

text: 17... Kxf7 18. Qxh7+ Kf6
zh: 17... Kxf7 18. Qxh7+ Kf6

text: The partnership finished off the game as follows:
zh: 执白的两位棋手这样结束了对局：

text: 19. Qh4+¹ Kg7 20. Re7+ Rf7 21. Qd4+ Kf8² 22. Qh8+ Kxe7 23. Re1+ Kd6 24. Qe5#.
zh: 19. Qh4+¹ Kg7 20. Re7+ Rf7 21. Qd4+ Kf8² 22. Qh8+ Kxe7 23. Re1+ Kd6 24. Qe5#.

text: ¹ 19. Qe7+ Kf5 20. Qxf8+ mates more quickly.
zh: ¹ 19. Qe7+ Kf5 20. Qxf8+能更快将杀。

text: ² Or 21... Kg8 22. Re8+ Rf8 23. Rxf8+ Kxf8 24. Qf6+ Kg8 25. Re1, etc.
zh: ² 或21... Kg8 22. Re8+ Rf8 23. Rxf8+ Kxf8 24. Qf6+ Kg8 25. Re1等。

text: Lasker came to grief in several games against Janowski through accepting sacrifices against his own principles. It is possible that Lasker was riled by the touch of impudence which can be seen in Janowski's moves and of which there was even more in his behaviour as a whole.
zh: 拉斯克在几盘对雅诺夫斯基的棋中，违背自己的原则接受弃子，结果遭遇败局。或许是雅诺夫斯基走法中那种略带挑衅的意味激怒了拉斯克；这种意味在雅诺夫斯基平日的言行中更加明显。

text: Complex focal-points
zh: 复合焦点

text: Just as a successful combination derives essentially from the multiple effects of single moves, so attacks on the castled king are also more likely to succeed if they are built up with the assistance of threats against a number of different squares. We shall find that in many attacks of this kind the attacker tries to corner the king by creating a second or even a third focal-point. There have already been cases of such complex focal-points in previous examples, but we shall now examine the matter more closely.
zh: 成功的组合，本质上往往来自一步棋的多重作用。同样，如果对王城的攻击借助了针对多个不同格子的威胁，也更容易成功。我们会发现，在许多这样的攻击中，进攻方试图通过制造第二个、甚至第三个焦点，把王逼入绝境。前面的例子中已经出现过这种复合焦点，现在进一步仔细讨论。

text: We have already mentioned the part played by secondary focal-points and by the combination of this kind of focal-point with a real one. However, here we will examine only the combining of two or more real focal-points, i.e. squares from which a player either actually mates or could do so in a variation. These real complex focal-points can be divided up as follows:
zh: 前面已经讨论过次要焦点的作用，以及它与真正将杀焦点的配合。不过，这里只讨论两个或更多真正将杀焦点的结合，也就是棋手实际在这些格子上将杀，或能在某条变化中从这里将杀。这种真正的复合焦点可以分为三类：

text:
1) The focal-points are adjacent squares of different colours (e.g. g7 and h7).
2) The focal-points are nearby squares of the same colour (e.g. h7 and f7).
3) The focal-points are of the same colour and make up a whole complex or network of squares (e.g. f6, g7 and h8).
zh:
1）焦点是相邻的异色格，例如g7和h7。
2）焦点是距离较近的同色格，例如h7和f7。
3）焦点属于同一颜色，并构成一整片格子网络，例如f6、g7和h8。

text: In general, one or more of the attacker's pieces control both focal-points, while the rest, in the course of the attack, transfer their influence from one focal-point to the other, preferably in the shortest time possible (i.e. one move). As far as simultaneous influence over two squares of different colours is concerned, for practical purposes only the queen comes into consideration, and in exceptional cases the rook; but if the focal-points are of the same colour, both the knight and, in particular, the bishop are effective. All the pieces are capable of transferring the attack from one focal-point to the other, though the bishop is unable to do this if the focal-points are of different colours. The bishop is, however, well suited to the case of focal-points of the same colour, while when the focal-points belong to the third group, it is indeed the classic piece by which the whole network is dominated.
zh: 一般而言，进攻方有一个或几个棋子同时控制两个焦点，其余棋子则在进攻过程中，把作用从一个焦点转移到另一个焦点，最好只用一步完成。若要同时作用于两个异色格，实战中主要依靠后，特殊情况下也可以用车；如果焦点是同色格，马和象都能发挥作用，尤其是象。各种棋子都能把攻击从一个焦点转移到另一个，但异色焦点是象的例外。对于同色焦点，象却十分适合；在第三类局面中，象更是统治整个格子网络的典型棋子。

text: When play is based on focal-points of different colours, the attack may be switched rapidly from one of the squares to the other. However, the commoner and more important cases are those in which there are two separate stages, the attack on the first focal-point being exhausted before the player transfers it decisively to the second. This transfer is often combined with a transformation of the mating pattern. An example of this is given in the following diagram (D).
zh: 围绕异色焦点展开战斗时，攻击可以迅速从一个格子转向另一个。不过，更常见也更重要的情况，是攻击分为两个阶段：第一个焦点上的手段已经用尽，进攻方才决定性地转向第二个焦点。这种转移往往伴随着将杀模式的变化。下图就是一个例子。

text: White, to move, begins with a sharp threat against the focal-point g7.
zh: 白方行棋，先对g7焦点制造一个尖锐的威胁。

text: 1. f6 Kh8
zh: 1. f6 Kh8

text: In order to be able to meet 2. Qh6 by 2... Rg8. 1... Qc6 is weaker because of 2. Rf3¹ and Black has only made his position worse.
zh: 准备用2... Rg8应对2. Qh6。1... Qc6较弱，因为有2. Rf3¹，黑方只是使自己的局面更糟。

text: ¹ 2. Qh6 forces immediate mate.
zh: ¹ 2. Qh6可立即强制将杀。

text: 2. Qh6 Rg8
zh: 2. Qh6 Rg8

text: White can clearly go no further in his threats against g7, but a new opportunity now offers itself — a rapid preparation for mate on h7, for which the queen is already excellently placed; all that is needed is to bring a rook on to the h-file.
zh: 显然，白方无法进一步加强对g7的威胁，但新的机会出现了：迅速准备在h7将杀。后已经处于极佳位置，只需把车调到h线上。

text: 3. Rf3! Bxf3
zh: 3. Rf3! Bxf3

text: Forced, since there was a threat not only of 4. Rh3 (against which, for example, 3... Qc6 would have helped²) but also of 4. Qxh7+ and 5. Rh3#.
zh: 被迫如此，因为白方不仅威胁4. Rh3（例如3... Qc6据说能应对这个威胁²），还威胁4. Qxh7+，接着5. Rh3#。

text: ² I cannot see why it would have helped.
zh: ² 我看不出这步为什么能起作用。

text: 4. gxf3 d5
zh: 4. gxf3 d5

text: The new threat of a queen sacrifice followed by Rh2# wipes out Black's defence. White does not play 5. Rh2 now, in which case Black would give up his queen for the rook, but **5. f4**, when Black can only stave off mate for a move or two by sacrificing his queen at f4.
zh: 新的威胁是先弃后，再Rh2#，黑方的防守因此瓦解。白方现在不走5. Rh2，否则黑方可以用后换掉车；而是走**5. f4**，黑方只能在f4弃后，把将杀拖延一两步。

text: In the following diagram we have an instructive example of play using focal-points of different colours. The threat against the focal-point h7 is replaced by one against g7. Then comes the decisive moment in the main variation — a sudden simultaneous attack on h7 and g7. In one sub-variation there even appears a third focal-point at f7.
zh: 下图是运用异色焦点的一个富有启发性的例子。针对h7焦点的威胁，转化为针对g7的威胁；随后主线中出现决定性的一刻：突然同时攻击h7和g7。在一个分支中，甚至还会出现第三个焦点f7。

text: 1. Rh1 Kg8!
zh: 1. Rh1 Kg8!

text: By 1... Bxg3+ 2. Ke2 Black would only make the defence more difficult for himself. In playing 1... Kg8! he attempts to defend by running with his king, i.e. he surrenders h7 to White and hopes for the continuation 2. Qxh7+? Kf8 3. Qh8+ Ke7, which leads to a complete consolidation of the black king's position; the tables are then turned and Black threatens ...Rc3 followed by play on the queenside against the weak spots in White's camp. Therefore, White does not capture on h7, but hits on a manoeuvre to open up the d3–h7 diagonal by the lethal f6.
zh: 1... Bxg3+ 2. Ke2只会让黑方更难防守。走1... Kg8!，是试图通过王逃跑来防守，也就是把h7让给白方，希望对局继续2. Qxh7+? Kf8 3. Qh8+ Ke7。这样黑王的位置就完全稳固了，局势反转，黑方威胁...Rc3，随后在后翼攻击白方阵地中的弱点。因此，白方不吃h7，而是找到一个调动，用致命的f6冲兵打开d3—h7斜线。

text: The passive 2. Rh3 would be weak, while 2. Rh4? is clearly no good because of 2... Bxg3+ and 3... Bxh4.
zh: 被动的2. Rh3较弱；2. Rh4?则明显不行，因为有2... Bxg3+，接着3... Bxh4。

text: The text move threatens 3. Rg5+ fxg5 4. f6 with the double threat of 5. Qg7# and 5. Bxh7+ Kh8 6. Bg6+ Kg8 7. Qh7+ Kf8 8. Qxf7#. This main variation, culminating in simultaneous threats against h7 and g7 can, it is true, be countered by 2... Qd6, but that allows 3. Qxh7+, 4. Qh8+, and 5. Qxc8, when White is a rook up. After 2... Bxg3+ 3. Ke2 Black can do nothing in the face of Rg5+ and f6. However, he discovers a subtle defence, which is typical for such positions.
zh: 实战这步威胁3. Rg5+ fxg5 4. f6，形成5. Qg7#和5. Bxh7+ Kh8 6. Bg6+ Kg8 7. Qh7+ Kf8 8. Qxf7#的双重威胁。这条主线最终同时威胁h7和g7；黑方确实可以用2... Qd6应对，但那样白方有3. Qxh7+、4. Qh8+、5. Qxc8，多出一车。2... Bxg3+ 3. Ke2之后，黑方面对Rg5+和f6也束手无策。不过，他找到了一种巧妙的防守，是此类局面中的典型手段。

text: This protects the third focal-point at f7, which is important as the final mating square in the combination beginning with 3. Rg5+; thus after 3... fxg5 4. f6 Bxf6 5. Bxh7+ there is no mate. But White still has one trump card left.
zh: 这步保护第三个焦点f7；在以3. Rg5+开始的组合中，f7作为最后的将杀格非常重要。这样3... fxg5 4. f6 Bxf6 5. Bxh7+之后，白方就没有将杀了。不过，白方还留着一张王牌。

text: Attacking Black's queen, which is overloaded with duties at the key square c7: it is obliged to guard the rook (against the possibility of Qxh7+ and Qh8+) and also watch the square f7. Black therefore played:
zh: 攻击黑后。黑后在关键格c7身负过多职责：既要保护车，以应对Qxh7+和Qh8+，又要照看f7格。因此黑方走：

text: If 3... Bxg3+, White would in this case have to play 4. Kf3!¹.
zh: 如果3... Bxg3+，白方在这里就必须走4. Kf3!¹。

text: ¹ Black should try 3... Qc1!, creating serious counter-threats and preventing 4. Rg5+ fxg5 5. f6 because of 5... Rc2+ 6. Bxc2 Qxc2+, followed by 7... Qg6. White should continue 4. Rh4 Rc2+ 5. Bxc2 Qxc2+ 6. Kg1 Qxf5 7. Qh5 with a large advantage, but of course there is no mate.
zh: ¹ 黑方应试走3... Qc1!，制造严重的反威胁，并阻止4. Rg5+ fxg5 5. f6，因为有5... Rc2+ 6. Bxc2 Qxc2+，接着7... Qg6。白方应继续4. Rh4 Rc2+ 5. Bxc2 Qxc2+ 6. Kg1 Qxf5 7. Qh5，取得很大优势，但当然没有将杀。

text: 4. Rh4
zh: 4. Rh4

text: A simple move and one which shows that Black's queen has yet another function — to maintain control of the b8–h2 diagonal. There is now an irresistible threat of Rg4+; 4... Bxg3+ 5. Kxg3 Qd6+ 6. Kf3 Qf8 is useless due to 7. Qxh7#.
zh: 简单的一步，却揭示了黑后的又一项职责：维持对b8—h2斜线的控制。现在Rg4+的威胁已经无法抵挡；4... Bxg3+ 5. Kxg3 Qd6+ 6. Kf3 Qf8也无济于事，因为有7. Qxh7#。

text: An excellent example of the shift of threats from one focal-point to another, and at the same time a lesson in the troubles facing a piece which is overburdened with different functions.
zh: 这是一个极好的例子，展示了威胁如何从一个焦点转移到另一个焦点，也说明一个棋子承担过多不同职责时会遇到怎样的困难。

text: In this position, from Szabo–van Scheltinga, Hilversum 1947, White won in interesting fashion.
zh: 下图来自1947年在希尔弗瑟姆的萨博对范谢尔廷加一局，白方以有趣的方式获胜。
caption_zh: 萨博（白）对范谢尔廷加（黑），白方行棋

text: 1. Ng5 g6 2. Nd5
zh: 1. Ng5 g6 2. Nd5

text: White's first move, with its attack on h7, forced a weakening on the long diagonal, and his subsequent manoeuvres aim to bring the queen to that diagonal.
zh: 白方第一步攻击h7，迫使黑方削弱了长斜线。随后的调动，就是为了把后送到这条斜线上。

text: 2... Qa3 3. Bxb5 axb5 4. Rc3 Qa5 5. e6! Nxe6 6. Rxe6 Bxe6 7. Qd4+ f6 8. Nxf6
zh: 2... Qa3 3. Bxb5 axb5 4. Rc3 Qa5 5. e6! Nxe6 6. Rxe6 Bxe6 7. Qd4+ f6 8. Nxf6

text: Now White threatens to decide the issue by Nh5+ and mate at the focal-point g7. Black's only answer is to attack the white queen.
zh: 现在白方威胁Nh5+，接着在g7焦点将杀，结束战斗。黑方唯一的应对，是攻击白后。

text: After 10... Qxe5 the attack returns to the original focal-point at h7 in the shape of 11. Rxh7#.
zh: 10... Qxe5之后，攻击又回到最初的h7焦点：11. Rxh7#。

text: This position arose in the game V. Vuković–Endzelins from the match between Yugoslavia and Latvia at the 1936 Munich Olympiad. White first obtained freedom of action for himself by blocking the long light diagonal.
zh: 下图出现在1936年慕尼黑奥林匹克团体赛南斯拉夫对拉脱维亚的比赛中，V.武科维奇对恩泽林斯一局。白方先堵住白格长斜线，为自己的行动争取自由。
caption_zh: V.武科维奇（白）对恩泽林斯（黑），白方行棋

text: 1. d5! exd5
zh: 1. d5! exd5

text: If 1... Nxd5, then 2. Qg5 g6 3. Bxg6, etc.
zh: 如果1... Nxd5，则2. Qg5 g6 3. Bxg6等。

text: 2. Ne2 Qe6 3. Bxg7! Kxg7 4. Qg5+ Kh8 5. Qh4+
zh: 2. Ne2 Qe6 3. Bxg7! Kxg7 4. Qg5+ Kh8 5. Qh4+

text: White checks from h4 rather than h6 to give Black the chance to make a mistake. Endzelins did in fact fall for it and played 5... Kg7?; this was followed by 6. Nd4, and Black lost his queen, since Nf5+ leads to a terrible catastrophe on the focal-point g7. The rest of the actual game is of no interest (it finished 6... Rg8 7. Qg5+ Kf8 8. Nxe6+ Ke7 9. Ng7 Rxg7 10. Qxg7 Rg8 11. Re1+ 1-0), but what does interest is an analysis of Black's more tenacious reply 5... Kg8 (D).
zh: 白方选择从h4而不是h6将军，给黑方一个犯错的机会。恩泽林斯果然上当，走了5... Kg7?；白方接着6. Nd4，黑方丢后，因为Nf5+会在g7焦点引发惨重灾难。实战余下部分已无讨论价值，最后是6... Rg8 7. Qg5+ Kf8 8. Nxe6+ Ke7 9. Ng7 Rxg7 10. Qxg7 Rg8 11. Re1+ 1-0。更值得分析的是黑方顽强的应招5... Kg8（见图）。
caption_zh: V.武科维奇（白）对恩泽林斯（黑），分析变化，白方行棋

text: Rellstab in his book of the tournament states that White would then have to satisfy himself with perpetual check, but this is not correct. Admittedly, after 6. Nd4 Rxc1! 7. Rxc1 Qe5 8. Nf5 Black has the reply 8... Ne4!, an interesting example of a move with a double defensive purpose with reference to the focal-points h7 and g7, around which White's attack revolves. Further attempts, e.g. by 9. Qg4+ Kh8 10. f3, are dangerous for White because of 10... Bc8!, while other short-cuts also have obstacles in their way. It was, however, White's intention to take the rook with his queen, and this would in fact have won the game, as the following analysis shows:
zh: 雷尔斯塔布在赛事专著中说，此时白方只能满足于长将，但这不正确。确实，6. Nd4 Rxc1! 7. Rxc1 Qe5 8. Nf5之后，黑方有8... Ne4!。这步很有趣，同时对围绕白方进攻的h7和g7两个焦点起到防守作用。白方若再尝试9. Qg4+ Kh8 10. f3等，会因10... Bc8!而遇到危险；其他捷径也都有障碍。不过，白方原本打算用后吃车，而以下分析表明，这样确实可以赢棋：

text: 6. Qg5+ Kh8 7. Qh6+ Kg8 8. Nd4 Rxc1 9. Qxc1! Qe5 10. Nf5
zh: 6. Qg5+ Kh8 7. Qh6+ Kg8 8. Nd4 Rxc1 9. Qxc1! Qe5 10. Nf5

text: There is now an attack on the two focal-points h7 and g7, combined in some variations with another on f7.
zh: 现在白方攻击h7和g7两个焦点，在一些变化中，还会加上对f7的攻击。

text: If Black plays 10... Ne4, there follows 11. Bxe4 dxe4 12. Qg5+ Kh8 13. Rd7! when Black has no proper defence against the threat of 14. Qh6+ and 15. Ne7+ winning his queen, e.g. if 13... Re8, then 14. Qh5+ Kg8 15. Qxf7+ mating.
zh: 如果黑方走10... Ne4，则11. Bxe4 dxe4 12. Qg5+ Kh8 13. Rd7!，威胁14. Qh6+，接着15. Ne7+得后，黑方没有有效防守。例如13... Re8，则14. Qh5+ Kg8 15. Qxf7+，将杀。

text: The only way to meet the threat of 12. Ne7+ and 13. Qxh7#.
zh: 这是应对12. Ne7+和13. Qxh7#威胁的唯一办法。

text: 12. Nd6! Bxd6
zh: 12. Nd6! Bxd6

text: Neither 12... Ng5 13. Nxe8 nor 12... Re7 13. Bxh7+ Kh8 14. Nf5 hold out any hope for Black.
zh: 无论12... Ng5 13. Nxe8，还是12... Re7 13. Bxh7+ Kh8 14. Nf5，黑方都没有希望。

text: **13. Bxh7+ Kh8 14. Bg6+** with the final mate on f7.
zh: **13. Bxh7+ Kh8 14. Bg6+**，最终在f7将杀。

text: Into the second group fall focal-points of the same colour which do not qualify as 'a network of squares'. The most typical case is that of h7 and f7, and in the next example we shall examine the most typical attack by the queen and bishop against these two squares.
zh: 第二类包括同色焦点，但还不足以构成一个格子网络。最典型的是h7和f7。下例将讨论后与象针对这两格发动的最典型攻击。

text: In the following diagram White begins with:
zh: 下图中，白方这样开始进攻：

text: 1. Qh5
zh: 1. Qh5

text: He is threatening to sacrifice his bishop on h6 because all the essential preconditions for such a sacrifice have been fulfilled, as will be seen from the following analysis. We shall examine those replies by Black which lead to the characteristic formation of white queen on h6 and bishop on the b1–h7 diagonal. We shall leave aside the replies 1... Qe6 and 1... f6, the first of which is bad because of 2. Bf5 and the second because of 2. Qg6.
zh: 白方威胁在h6弃象；这种弃象所需的全部基本条件已经具备，以下分析会说明这一点。我们将讨论黑方那些会导致典型子力配置的应招：白后在h6，白象在b1—h7斜线上。暂不讨论1... Qe6和1... f6，因为前者有2. Bf5，后者有2. Qg6，都不好。

text: First of all, the naive capture 1... Qxb4?. This is defeated by the sacrifice 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6, threatening mate on h7. This could be parried by 3... Re8, but Black then has to pay for the unprotected focal-point at f7 after 4. Bh7+ Kh8 5. Bg6+ Kg8 6. Qh7+ Kf8 7. Qxf7#.
zh: 先看天真的吃兵1... Qxb4?。白方用2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6弃象，威胁在h7将杀，就能击败这步。3... Re8可以暂时防住这个威胁，但4. Bh7+ Kh8 5. Bg6+ Kg8 6. Qh7+ Kf8 7. Qxf7#之后，黑方就要为无人保护的f7焦点付出代价。

text: We have seen that the square f7 must be protected by the queen, since the rook on f8 has to move after the sacrifice, which suggests 1... Nb6 or 1... Na7. These too are answered by 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6, and if 3... Re8, then 4. Qh7+ and 5. Qh8#; nor is there any future in 3... f6 4. exf6 Rxf6 5. Rxe7 Rxh6 6. Rxb7.
zh: 我们已经看到，弃象之后f8车必须移动，所以f7格必须由后保护。这提示黑方可以考虑1... Nb6或1... Na7。但白方仍应以2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6；如果3... Re8，则4. Qh7+，接着5. Qh8#。3... f6 4. exf6 Rxf6 5. Rxe7 Rxh6 6. Rxb7也没有前途。

text: Black realizes that his queen is not well placed on e7 because it blocks this escape square and thus enables White to mate with his queen on h8. Black can try to move his queen away, but in such a way that it still protects the focal-point f7: 1... Qc7 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 Re8 (or 3... f6 4. exf6, with the decisive threat of 5. Re7) 4. Rac1 Qd7 5. Bh7+ Kh8 6. Bf5+ and White wins the queen.
zh: 黑方意识到，后在e7位置不好，堵住了王的逃跑格，让白后可以在h8将杀。他可以试着移开后，同时仍保护f7焦点：1... Qc7 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 Re8（或3... f6 4. exf6，威胁决定性的5. Re7）4. Rac1 Qd7 5. Bh7+ Kh8 6. Bf5+，白方得后。

text: From this it can be seen that Black's queen could not even have gone to d7 on the first move.
zh: 由此也可以看出，黑后第一步就到d7，同样不行。

text: We can now cut our speculation short; there only remain 1... Re8 and 1... Rd8. That 1... Rd8 is no good can be seen after 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6, since then 3... Qe6 cannot be played because of 4. Qg5+.
zh: 现在可以缩小考虑范围，只剩1... Re8和1... Rd8。2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6就说明1... Rd8不好，因为有4. Qg5+，黑方不能再走3... Qe6。

text: Thus we arrive at the main variation:
zh: 于是我们得到主线：

text: After this move the sacrifice of the bishop on h6 is somewhat more complicated, but it is still White's best continuation. On the other hand, 2. Bf4 is also good; less useful here (as on the first move) is 2. Qg4 because of 2... Kh8 3. Qxd4 Rd8 4. Qc3 Nb6 and Black can hold his own.
zh: 这步之后，h6弃象稍微复杂一些，但仍是白方最佳的后续手段。2. Bf4也不错。与第一步一样，2. Qg4在这里效果较差，因为2... Kh8 3. Qxd4 Rd8 4. Qc3 Nb6，黑方能维持局面。

text: 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 Qe6
zh: 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 Qe6

text: This is the right reply. After 4. Bh7+ Kh8 White now gets nowhere by 5. Bg6+, while the other discovered checks fail because White's queen is attacked by Black's; furthermore, if 5. Qh5, Black has the reply 5... Kg7 6. Bf5 Qh6 with an adequate defence.
zh: 正确的应招。4. Bh7+ Kh8之后，白方现在走5. Bg6+无济于事；其他闪将也不行，因为白后受到黑后的攻击。此外，如果5. Qh5，黑方有5... Kg7 6. Bf5 Qh6，可以有效防守。

text: White's later play is interesting, even if it is no longer as typical of this kind of attack as the possibilities cited hitherto.
zh: 白方接下来的走法很有趣，虽然不像前面列出的那些可能性那样，能典型地代表这种攻击。

text: 4. Qh7+ Kf8 5. Bf5 (D)
zh: 4. Qh7+ Kf8 5. Bf5 (D)

text: White's queen is now best placed where it is, on h7; further checks would only make it easier for Black to defend himself.
zh: 白后现在留在h7最好；继续将军只会让黑方更容易防守。

text: After 5... Qd5 6. Qh6+ Black cannot play 6... Kg8 due to 7. Bh7+ and 8. Be4+, while 6... Ke7 7. Be4 wins the black bishop, for 7... Qd7 is defeated by 8. e6.
zh: 5... Qd5 6. Qh6+之后，黑方不能走6... Kg8，因为有7. Bh7+和8. Be4+；6... Ke7 7. Be4则会丢象，因为7... Qd7会被8. e6击败。

text: 5... Qb6 is of no use either, since 6. Rac1! leaves Black without a reasonable reply, e.g. if 6... Ne7, then 7. e6 fxe6 8. Bxe6 is quickly decisive.
zh: 5... Qb6也没用，因为6. Rac1!之后黑方没有像样的应招。例如6... Ne7，则7. e6 fxe6 8. Bxe6，很快决定胜负。

text: **6. Be4 Qb6 7. Bxb7 Qxb7 8. e6** and White wins. The threat is 9. Qh8+ Ke7 10. exf7+ and the reply 8... Nd6 fails against 9. e7+ and 10. Qh8#.
zh: **6. Be4 Qb6 7. Bxb7 Qxb7 8. e6**，白方获胜。威胁是9. Qh8+ Ke7 10. exf7+；8... Nd6会遭到9. e7+，接着10. Qh8#。

text: This analysis shows what great power there is in the formation of queen at h6 and bishop at d3 when combined with a rook at e1 and a pawn at e5. The various operations connected with the focal-points h7 and f7 are well worth remembering, since opportunities to use them arise frequently in actual games. Since the defender must move his rook from f8 when mate is threatened at h7, it is clearly a decisive factor whether or not the focal-point f7 is protected by other pieces. An alternative defence involves ...f6 or ...f5, but the success of such a reply depends on the other features of the position, which must be carefully assessed.
zh: 这些分析表明，h6后、d3象，配合e1车和e5兵，威力有多么强大。围绕h7和f7焦点的各种手段非常值得记住，实战中经常会出现运用它们的机会。面对h7的将杀威胁，防守方必须把车从f8移开，因此f7焦点是否有其他棋子保护，显然是决定性的因素。另一种防守是...f6或...f5，但这样的应招能否成功，取决于局面的其他特点，必须仔细评估。

text: The main feature of the third group is the network of weak squares of the same colour; here the attacker's bishop is, as a rule, the piece which controls the focal-points permanently, while the others are used for manoeuvring purposes. It should be noted that control over a network of squares is also an important factor in positional play, but in attacks on the castled king it is particularly effective. The reason for this is a positional one, since control over a network is often of a fairly permanent nature.
