The most essential precondition is to 'clear' the network not only of the influence of the opponent's bishop (either by eliminating it or driving it away) but also of possible resistance from the opponent's pawns at important points in the network.
zh: 第三类的主要特点，是同色弱格构成一个网络。通常由进攻方的象持续控制各个焦点，其他棋子则负责调动。应当指出，控制格子网络在局面战中也是重要因素，但在攻击王城时尤其有效。其原因在于局面本身：对这种网络的控制，往往能相当持久。最基本的前提，是“清除”对方象对这片网络的影响，或把它消灭，或将它赶走；同时还要消除对方兵在网络中重要格子上可能形成的抵抗。

text: When the attacker has 'cleared' the network and fixed the position, the attacking operation proper follows; the squares which are candidate focal-points can easily be determined, while the other squares in the network may serve as secondary focal-points or else as strong squares for the attacker to post his pieces on.
zh: 进攻方“清除”这片网络并固定局面之后，真正的攻击行动便随之展开。哪些格子可能成为焦点，很容易确定；网络中的其他格子，则可以充当次要焦点，或供进攻方安置棋子的强格。

text: In the above diagram the network of dark squares is already 'cleared' and covered by White's bishop, which is firmly installed at f6. The network consists of the squares f6, g7 and h8, and also the connected squares f8 and h6. The squares g7 and h8 are candidates as focal-points, f6 is a strong square for the attacker's pieces while f8 and h6 can serve as secondary focal-points or strong squares. All this concentration of white power encircles the unfortunate black king, which has no real prospect of extricating itself from the net and escaping to the queenside, since e7 is also controlled by White. Black does not even have a dark-squared bishop to provide resistance on the network, and because of the blocked position in the centre he cannot undertake a counterattack; he is confined to defending himself. The only minor piece he has left is a knight, but this piece can in fact exercise considerable defensive influence in positions of this kind.
zh: 上图中，黑格网络已经被“清除”，并受到牢牢驻扎在f6的白象控制。这片网络包括f6、g7、h8，以及与它们相连的f8和h6。g7和h8可能成为焦点，f6是进攻方棋子的强格，f8和h6则可作次要焦点或强格。白方集中起来的力量包围了不幸的黑王；由于e7也被白方控制，黑王实际上没有什么希望挣脱这张网、逃到后翼。黑方连一枚能在这片网络中抵抗的黑格象都没有；中心又被封闭，无法发动反击，只能防守。他唯一剩下的轻子是马，但在这种局面中，马其实能发挥相当大的防守作用。

text: If White's domination is based on a dark-square network, Black still has one thing on which he can logically rely — the solid structure of his position on the light squares. In some such cases the success of an attack depends on the ability to break down resistance on the light squares by means of a sacrifice. This feature appears in the analysis of the above position, which, by virtue of its simplicity and its typical character, will well repay study.
zh: 白方的控制既然建立在黑格网络之上，黑方便仍有一个可以合理依靠的条件：自己在白格上的稳固结构。在一些这样的局面中，攻击能否成功，就取决于能否通过弃子打破白格上的抵抗。上图的分析会展示这一特点；这个局面简单而典型，很值得研究。

text: It is Black's move, and his first concern is to provide a defence against White's manoeuvre Qd2–h6, which threatens to bring about disaster on the focal-point g7. Various attempts at defence by Black and attacking stratagems by White, all of them typical and consequently instructive, will now be examined in a series of continuations.
zh: 轮到黑方走，他首先要防住白方Qd2—h6的调动，否则g7焦点就会遭受灾难。下面用一系列变化讨论黑方的各种防守尝试，以及白方相应的攻击手段。这些方法都很典型，因而很有启发性。

text: Black is contemplating a defensive system with his king on h7 and his knight on g8, which could be reached after, say, 2. Qd2 Kh7 3. Re3 Ne7 4. Rh3 Ng8. White can then assert his superiority by 5. Bg5 h5 6. g4, but 1... h6 can be better punished as follows:
zh: 黑方考虑把王放到h7、马放到g8，组成一个防守体系，例如2. Qd2 Kh7 3. Re3 Ne7 4. Rh3 Ng8之后。白方接着5. Bg5 h5 6. g4，可以发挥优势；不过，以下手段能更有力地惩罚1... h6：

text: 2. Re3! Kh7 3. Rh3 Ne7 4. Rxh6+! Kxh6 5. Qg4 Kh7 6. Qh3+ Kg8 7. Qh8#.
zh: 2. Re3! Kh7 3. Rh3 Ne7 4. Rxh6+! Kxh6 5. Qg4 Kh7 6. Qh3+ Kg8 7. Qh8#.

text: Here we see the part played by the focal-points at h6 and h8.
zh: 这里展示了h6和h8两个焦点的作用。

text: Forced, as White threatened mate by 3. Qh6; if 2... Kf8, then 3. Qh6+ also mates.
zh: 被迫如此，因为白方威胁3. Qh6将杀；如果2... Kf8，则3. Qh6+同样将杀。

text: 3. Qg5
zh: 3. Qg5

text: The simplest answer, as it prevents ...Ne7 for a decisive tempo. Also good is 3. g4, for 3... hxg4 is met by 4. Qg5 and mate. If 3. Re3, Black can defend himself more stubbornly with 3... Ne7 4. Rh3 Nf5 5. g4 Nh6 followed by 6... Rg8.
zh: 最简单的办法，阻止...Ne7，赢得决定性的一个先手。3. g4也好，因为3... hxg4会遭到4. Qg5并将杀。如果3. Re3，黑方便可以用3... Ne7 4. Rh3 Nf5 5. g4 Nh6，接着6... Rg8，更顽强地防守。

text: 3... Rc7 4. Re3 Ne7 5. Rh3 Nf5
zh: 3... Rc7 4. Re3 Ne7 5. Rh3 Nf5

text: Otherwise White mates by 6. Rxh5+!.
zh: 否则白方用6. Rxh5+!将杀。

text: 6. g4 Rg8
zh: 6. g4 Rg8

text: Or 6... Nh6 7. Rxh5, etc.
zh: 或6... Nh6 7. Rxh5等。

text: 7. gxf5 gxf5 8. Rxh5#.
zh: 7. gxf5 gxf5 8. Rxh5#.

text: In this example it is the resistance on the light squares that is overcome.
zh: 这个例子中，被打破的是白格上的抵抗。

text: Black's queen is hoping to defend from f8.
zh: 黑后希望从f8进行防守。

text: **2. Re3 Qf8 3. Rh3 h6 4. Qd2 Kh7 5. Bg5 h5 6. Qe2 Ne7 7. Rxh5+! gxh5 8. Qxh5+ Kg8 9. Bf6 Ng6 10. Re1**, and Black has no answer to the threat of Re3–h3 followed by Qh8+ and mate. This is an important mating pattern in such positions.
zh: **2. Re3 Qf8 3. Rh3 h6 4. Qd2 Kh7 5. Bg5 h5 6. Qe2 Ne7 7. Rxh5+! gxh5 8. Qxh5+ Kg8 9. Bf6 Ng6 10. Re1**，白方威胁Re3—h3，接着Qh8+并将杀，黑方无法应对。这是此类局面中的一个重要将杀模式。

text: D) 1... Ne7 2. Qd2 Qe8
zh: D) 1... Ne7 2. Qd2 Qe8

text: Or 2... Nf5 3. g4 Ng7 4. Qh6 Ne8 5. Re3, threatening both 6. Rh3 and 6. Qxh7+.
zh: 或2... Nf5 3. g4 Ng7 4. Qh6 Ne8 5. Re3，同时威胁6. Rh3和6. Qxh7+。

text: 3. Re3 Qf8 4. Rh3 Rc7
zh: 3. Re3 Qf8 4. Rh3 Rc7

text: This position can also arise in variation C.
zh: 这一局面也可能从变化C中出现。

text: 5. Qg5 b5 6. Qh4
zh: 5. Qg5 b5 6. Qh4

text: White may also play 6. g4, 7. Rh6, and 8. Qh4.
zh: 白方也可以走6. g4、7. Rh6、8. Qh4。

text: **6... h5 7. Qg5 Kh7 8. Rxh5+! gxh5 9. Qxh5+ Qh6 10. Qxf7+** and mate. Yet another instructive mating pattern!
zh: **6... h5 7. Qg5 Kh7 8. Rxh5+! gxh5 9. Qxh5+ Qh6 10. Qxf7+**，将杀。又是一个富有启发性的将杀模式！

text: The black king tries to slip out of the net via e8.
zh: 黑王试图经e8溜出杀网。

text: 2. Qd2 Ke8 3. Qh6 Ne7 (D)
zh: 2. Qd2 Ke8 3. Qh6 Ne7 (D)

text: Or 3... Nd8 4. Qxh7 Qa4 5. Qg8+ Kd7 6. Qf8 with a decisive attack on the new focal-point at e7.
zh: 或3... Nd8 4. Qxh7 Qa4 5. Qg8+ Kd7 6. Qf8，对新焦点e7发起决定性的攻击。

text: 4. Qxh7 Qa4 5. Re3
zh: 4. Qxh7 Qa4 5. Re3

text: At this point White gains nothing from checking, but must instead bring his rook to f3.
zh: 此时白方将军没有收获，而必须把车调到f3。

text: 5... Qc2 6. Rf3 Qxb2 7. Rf1 Qa3
zh: 5... Qc2 6. Rf3 Qxb2 7. Rf1 Qa3

text: This parries the threat of 8. Bxe7, but now 8. Bg5 Nf5 9. g4 decides the game. In this variation the black king wriggled out to the edge of the network of weak dark squares, but even there he met his fate, its cause being the last square in the network, e7.
zh: 这步防住了8. Bxe7的威胁，但现在8. Bg5 Nf5 9. g4便决定胜负。这条变化中，黑王挣扎着逃到黑格弱格网络的边缘，却仍在那里遭遇厄运；使他败亡的，是这片网络的最后一格e7。

text: We shall not leave the above diagram yet, because a feature of very great practical importance should be pointed out. This is the benefit derived by White from the action of his rook on the h-file. Without an opportunity of making the manoeuvre Re3–h3, White cannot take Black's position by storm, because he lacks a threat against h7; if this does not exist, Black does not have to weaken his position, since he can easily ward off the threats against g7 alone. So even in this case, where there is a definite 'same-colour network', there is still a part to be played by alternative focal-points on squares of different colours (h7 or f7), and this applies in most practical cases. The weaknesses on the squares of the network are usually only the more sensitive ones, which does not mean that squares of the other colour will necessarily be safe — the king may succumb on them too!
zh: 暂且还不离开前面的局面，因为有一个极具实战意义的特点必须指出：白车在h线上发挥作用，给白方带来了好处。如果没有Re3—h3的调动机会，白方就无法强攻攻破黑方阵地，因为他缺少对h7的威胁。没有这个威胁，黑方就不必削弱自己的局面，只针对g7的威胁很容易挡住。因此，即使在这样明确存在“同色格网络”的局面中，另一颜色上的备选焦点，如h7或f7，仍能发挥作用。大多数实战局面都是如此。网络中的弱格通常只是更敏感的弱点，并不意味着另一颜色的格子一定安全——王也可能在那里被将杀！

text: We have noted the important part played by the rook on the h-file in the variations above, and we shall now go on to examine how positions of this kind can be exploited if there is no chance of employing a rook. Suppose that we move White's h-pawn from h2 to h4 in the above diagram; this gives a new situation of a type which often arises in practice, for the h-pawn is frequently advanced during the game. The pawn's being on h4 considerably blunts White's attack, and 1. h4? in the diagrammed position would be a poor move. Nevertheless, even with the pawn on h4 White has the better game, although he can only exploit his advantage slowly and Black retains chances of attacking on the queenside. Indeed, if Black's position on that side were a little further advanced, one could conclude that he would be able to preserve the balance. However, as things stand White is still the stronger, and we shall examine one continuation arising out of the new situation.
zh: 上面的变化已经说明车在h线上的重要作用。现在来看，若暂时无法用车沿h线进攻，该怎样利用这类局面。假设把前面图中白方的h兵从h2移到h4，就得到一种实战中经常出现的新情况，因为h兵在对局中常常会冲起。兵在h4明显削弱了白方的攻势，因此原图中的1. h4?是一步坏棋。不过，即使兵在h4，白方仍然较好，只是必须慢慢发挥优势，而黑方保留着在后翼进攻的机会。如果黑方在后翼的行动再领先一些，甚至可以判断他有能力维持平衡。但在现有局面中，白方仍然更强。下面分析这种新情况下的一条变化。

text: The modified diagram (with the pawn on h4) is given on the following page.
zh: 兵移到h4后的局面见下图（原书图在下一页）。

text: In this case too White's rook belongs on h3, even though his attack along the h-file is only a 'thing of the future'.
zh: 这里白车同样应放到h3，尽管沿h线的攻击还是“将来的事”。

text: 4... h5 would be to White's advantage, since it would simplify his task of opening up the g- and h-files, for example 5. g4 hxg4 6. Rh2 a5 7. h5 followed by 8. hxg6 (but not 8. h6? because of 8... Kh7, and Black is at once in a safe position!) with a decisive attack.
zh: 4... h5对白方有利，因为这让他更容易打开g线和h线，例如5. g4 hxg4 6. Rh2 a5 7. h5，接着8. hxg6，取得决定性攻势。但不能走8. h6?，因为8... Kh7之后，黑方立即安全了！

text: White's plan, a typical one in positions of this kind, is to play Kg2 and then Rah1. The immediate 6. hxg6 would be weaker, for Black would reply 6... fxg6 opening up the second rank for defensive purposes. White must first of all post his heavy pieces in their assault positions and only then venture on hxg6.
zh: 白方的计划是先Kg2，再Rah1，这是此类局面中的典型计划。立即6. hxg6较弱，因为黑方可以应以6... fxg6，打开自己的第二横线用于防守。白方必须先把重子配置到攻击位置，然后才能走hxg6。

text: Otherwise Black obtains good prospects with ...a3.
zh: 否则黑方冲起a3，就会取得良好前景。

text: 7... bxc3 8. bxc3 (D)
zh: 7... bxc3 8. bxc3 (D)

text: A raid by a black rook along the b-file will not succeed, since both rooks are needed to defend the second rank, as can be seen from the following variation: 8... Rab8 9. Kg2 Rb3 10. Rah1 Rc7 11. Qg5 Rxa3 (or 11... Qxa3 12. Qh6 Qf8 13. Qxh7+ Kxh7 14. hxg6+ Kxg6 15. Rh5 and mate) 12. hxg6 fxg6 13. Rxh7 Rxh7 14. Qxg6+ Rg7 15. Bxg7 Qxg7 16. Qe8+ and White wins. Black could, it is true, play 11... Rb2, in which case the above combination would not work; however, it would not stop the manoeuvre Rh4–f4.
zh: 黑车沿b线突袭不会成功，因为两车都需要防守黑方的第二横线。以下变化就能说明这一点：8... Rab8 9. Kg2 Rb3 10. Rah1 Rc7 11. Qg5 Rxa3（或11... Qxa3 12. Qh6 Qf8 13. Qxh7+ Kxh7 14. hxg6+ Kxg6 15. Rh5，将杀）12. hxg6 fxg6 13. Rxh7 Rxh7 14. Qxg6+ Rg7 15. Bxg7 Qxg7 16. Qe8+，白方获胜。黑方确实可以走11... Rb2，那样上述组合就不成立；但仍无法阻止Rh4—f4的调动。

text: 9. Qg5 Nb3 10. Re1 Rc7
zh: 9. Qg5 Nb3 10. Re1 Rc7

text: Clearly, 10... h6 is bad because of 11. hxg6.
zh: 显然10... h6不好，因为有11. hxg6。

text: 11. Kg2 Raa7 12. Reh1 Rab7 13. Rh4! Rd7 14. Rf4 Rdc7
zh: 11. Kg2 Raa7 12. Reh1 Rab7 13. Rh4! Rd7 14. Rf4 Rdc7

text: Black is unable to parry the combination which White has prepared. If White had previously made an incorrect exchange on g6, ...Qe8 would now be the answer to everything; in the present position this move would be answered by 15. Qh6 Qf8 16. Qxh7+ Kxh7 17. hxg6+ Kxg6 18. Rg4+ Kf5 19. Rh5+ Kxg4 20. Rg5#.
zh: 黑方无法防住白方准备好的组合。如果白方之前错误地在g6兑换，此时...Qe8就能应对一切；但在当前局面中，这步会遭到15. Qh6 Qf8 16. Qxh7+ Kxh7 17. hxg6+ Kxg6 18. Rg4+ Kf5 19. Rh5+ Kxg4 20. Rg5#。

text: **15. hxg6 fxg6 16. Qxg6+! hxg6 17. Rh8+ Kf7 18. Bd8+** and White finally wins.
zh: **15. hxg6 fxg6 16. Qxg6+! hxg6 17. Rh8+ Kf7 18. Bd8+**，白方终于获胜。

text: It is well worth remembering this analysis, especially the method of delaying the attack with the h-pawn and how the winning position is prepared by a calculated deployment of the pieces. The reader will be reminded of this extremely important practical technique in the section on the role of the rook files in the attack on the castled king.
zh: 这些分析很值得记住，尤其是延后h兵进攻的方法，以及如何通过精心配置子力来准备胜势。讨论a线、h线在王城攻击中作用的那一节，还会再次提醒读者注意这一极为重要的实战技巧。

text: As for the part played by the network of weak squares in attacks on the castled king, one more diagram and one interesting master game will be given as examples.
zh: 关于弱格网络在王城攻击中的作用，我们再给出一个局面和一盘有趣的大师对局。

text: This position is from the game Euwe–Flohr, Amsterdam 1939. White's bishop has reached the square f6, but the network is still guarded by the opponent's dark-squared bishop, which is preparing to effect a delayed fianchetto by ...Bg7. For this reason forceful play by White is indicated.
zh: 下图来自1939年在阿姆斯特丹的尤伟对弗洛尔一局。白象已经到达f6，但对方黑格象仍在守护这片网络，并准备通过...Bg7完成延后的侧翼出象。因此，白方应当采取强有力的行动。
caption_zh: 尤伟（白）对弗洛尔（黑），白方行棋

text: With the idea of eliminating the dark-squared bishop. If Black plays 1... Bxc5, then 2. dxc5 uncovers an attack on the bishop at d7, which Black cannot defend, e.g. if 2... Qc7, the manoeuvre Qe3–h6 is decisive.
zh: 构想是消灭黑格象。如果黑方走1... Bxc5，则2. dxc5打开对d7象的攻击，黑方无法保护它；例如2... Qc7，Qe3—h6的调动就能决定胜负。

text: If 2... gxh5, then 3. Qg3+ wins, while 2... Bg7 is answered by 3. Bxg7 Kxg7 4. Rxh7+ Kxh7 5. Qxf7+, followed by 6. Rd3. Also interesting is 2... h6 3. e5! Kh7 4. Qe3 Qxb2 5. Rd3 Qb1+ 6. Bf1 g5 (if 6... gxh5, then 7. Qe4+ and 8. Rg3+ wins; otherwise Black is mated by 7. Rxh6+ Bxh6 8. Qxh6+ Kxh6 9. Rh3#) 7. Qe4+ Kg8 8. Rxg5+ hxg5 9. Rh3, etc. The move played parries the threat of 3. Qh3.
zh: 如果2... gxh5，则3. Qg3+获胜；2... Bg7会遭到3. Bxg7 Kxg7 4. Rxh7+ Kxh7 5. Qxf7+，接着6. Rd3。另一个有趣的变化是2... h6 3. e5! Kh7 4. Qe3 Qxb2 5. Rd3 Qb1+ 6. Bf1 g5（如果6... gxh5，则7. Qe4+，接着8. Rg3+获胜；否则黑方会被7. Rxh6+ Bxh6 8. Qxh6+ Kxh6 9. Rh3#将杀）7. Qe4+ Kg8 8. Rxg5+ hxg5 9. Rh3等。实战走法防住了3. Qh3的威胁。

text: 3. dxe5 Be6 4. Qf4 Qxb2 5. Bf1 Be7
zh: 3. dxe5 Be6 4. Qf4 Qxb2 5. Bf1 Be7

text: He still cannot play 5... Bg7, because of 6. Bxg7 and 7. Qh6+.
zh: 黑方仍不能走5... Bg7，因为有6. Bxg7，接着7. Qh6+。

text: 6. Qh4
zh: 6. Qh4

text: Euwe notes in his commentary that Black's queen is fairly well placed on b2 (by controlling f2 and f6 it prevents Qh6 being played at once) and cites as more precise 6. Rb1 Qd4 (if 6... Qxb1, then 7. Qh6) 7. Rb4! Qd8 8. Qh4, etc. 6. Rd3 would also win more quickly than the move played.
zh: 尤伟在评注中指出，黑后在b2位置相当好：它控制f2和f6，阻止白方立即Qh6。他给出更精确的6. Rb1 Qd4（如果6... Qxb1，则7. Qh6）7. Rb4! Qd8 8. Qh4等。6. Rd3也比实战这步赢得更快。

text: The great defensive master's last trump: 7. Rxh7? is now no good because of 7... Qxf2+. Even so, Black is lost; the process merely takes a little longer.
zh: 这位伟大的防守大师亮出最后一张王牌：现在7. Rxh7?不行了，因为有7... Qxf2+。即便如此，黑方仍是败势，只是落败的过程稍长一些。

text: 7. Rh6 a5
zh: 7. Rh6 a5

text: If 7... Bg4, then 8. Rd3 with the threat of 9. Re3!.
zh: 如果7... Bg4，则8. Rd3，威胁9. Re3!。

text: 8. Rd3 Bxf2+
zh: 8. Rd3 Bxf2+

text: Otherwise White will play 9. Rf3.
zh: 否则白方就走9. Rf3。

text: 9. Qxf2 Qxf2+ 10. Kxf2 (D)
zh: 9. Qxf2 Qxf2+ 10. Kxf2 (D)
caption_zh: 尤伟（白）对弗洛尔（黑），黑方行棋

text: The situation now becomes critical; White must get his rook to h3 before Black's pawn promotes to a queen.
zh: 现在到了关键时刻：白方必须在黑兵升后之前，把车调到h3。

text: If 10... Ra6, there is insufficient time for 11. Be2 because of ...Rb6–b3, nor is 11. Rf3 Rb6 12. Rf4 strong enough owing to 12... g5! 13. Rf5 Rc8, and the black king escapes to d7. Strongest, after 10... Ra6, is 11. g4 Bxg4 12. Bh3!, etc.
zh: 如果10... Ra6，由于有...Rb6—b3，白方来不及走11. Be2。11. Rf3 Rb6 12. Rf4也不够强，因为12... g5! 13. Rf5 Rc8，黑王可以逃到d7。10... Ra6之后，最强的是11. g4 Bxg4 12. Bh3!等。

text: White can also win by 11. g4 Bxg4 12. Bh3. After the text move Black cannot reply 11... a3 because of 12. g4 a2 13. Rxh7, so he tries to prolong the game by a desperate rook sacrifice.
zh: 白方也可以用11. g4 Bxg4 12. Bh3获胜。实战这步之后，黑方不能应以11... a3，因为有12. g4 a2 13. Rxh7，于是他孤注一掷地弃车，试图延长对局。

text: 11... Ra5 12. g4 Rxe5 13. Bxe5 Bc4 14. Rdh3 Bxe2 15. Bf6 Re6 16. e5 Bxg4 17. Rxh7 Rxf6+ 18. exf6 1-0
zh: 11... Ra5 12. g4 Rxe5 13. Bxe5 Bc4 14. Rdh3 Bxe2 15. Bf6 Re6 16. e5 Bxg4 17. Rxh7 Rxf6+ 18. exf6 1-0

text: The rook has no difficulty in controlling the pawns, e.g. 18... Bxh3 19. Rxh3 b5 20. Rc3 b4 21. Rxc6 b3 22. Rb6, etc.
zh: 车控制这些兵毫无困难，例如18... Bxh3 19. Rxh3 b5 20. Rc3 b4 21. Rxc6 b3 22. Rb6等。

text:
Pilnik – Najdorf
Mar del Plata, 1942
Caro-Kann Defence
zh:
皮尔尼克—纳伊多夫
1942年，马德普拉塔
卡罗—卡恩防御

text: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6
zh: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6

text: Sounder is 4... Bf5 or 4... Nd7 followed by ...Ngf6.
zh: 更稳健的是4... Bf5，或4... Nd7，接着...Ngf6。

text: 5. Nxf6+ exf6
zh: 5. Nxf6+ exf6

text: The doubling of the pawns on the f-file represents a slight weakness in Black's position whichever pawn he recaptures with.
zh: 无论黑方用哪个兵吃回，f线叠兵都会使他的局面略有弱点。

text: 6. c3 Bd6 7. Bd3 O-O 8. Qh5
zh: 6. c3 Bd6 7. Bd3 O-O 8. Qh5

text: Black could answer this with 8... f5 (9. Bxf5? g6) and so ward off White's attack without weakening his castled position. Indeed, 8... f5 not only avoids weakening Black's position, it also falls in with his correct positional plan, i.e. the front f-pawn is used to control squares on the e-file, while the back one (at f7) stays at home and guards any weaknesses which the front one leaves behind it. If the front pawn is exchanged in some tussle over a square, Black has got rid of the doubled pawns and the fear of an inferior ending.
zh: 黑方可以应以8... f5（9. Bxf5? g6），在不削弱王城的情况下挡住白方的攻击。事实上，8... f5不仅避免削弱局面，还符合黑方正确的局面计划：用前面的f兵控制e线上的格子，后面的f7兵则留守，保护前兵冲起后留下的弱点。如果前兵在争夺某个格子的战斗中被兑换掉，黑方便摆脱了叠兵，也不必再担心不利的残局。

text: 8. Qc2 was sounder.
zh: 8. Qc2更稳健。

text: Though less precise than 8... f5 this is still not a mistake.
zh: 虽然不如8... f5精确，但这步还不算错误。

caption_zh: 白方走完9. Qh4后的局面

text: Fundamentally inappropriate, since White is stronger on the queenside and in particular has a firm hold on d4. Black should have left any operations on the queen's wing to White and instead prepared for ...f5 and ...Nd7–f6, but without exchanging queens and without relinquishing the d8–h4 diagonal to White. Correct, therefore, was 9... Nd7 10. Ne2 Be7! 11. O-O f5 12. Qg3 Nf6, etc.
zh: 这步从根本上不合适，因为白方在后翼更强，尤其牢牢控制着d4。黑方应把后翼行动留给白方，自己转而准备...f5和...Nd7—f6，但不要兑后，也不要把d8—h4斜线让给白方。因此，正确的是9... Nd7 10. Ne2 Be7! 11. O-O f5 12. Qg3 Nf6等。

text: Black should have played 11... Re8. At this point ...f5 is weak.
zh: 黑方应走11... Re8。此时...f5是软着。

text: By exchanging queens White could have obtained the better endgame prospects. However, why should he play for an endgame when he has the opportunity to gain control of the diagonal h4–d8, thereby obtaining the necessary conditions for an attack on the castled king based on a network of weak dark squares?
zh: 白方兑后可以得到更好的残局前景。不过，既然有机会控制h4—d8斜线，具备以黑格弱格网络为基础攻击王城的必要条件，为什么还要转入残局呢？

text: The diagonal cannot be defended: if 12... Be7, then 13. Bxe7 Nxe7 14. dxc5 Qxd3 15. Qxe7 while 12... f6 13. Bc4+ Kh8 14. Bh6 is equally unacceptable¹.
zh: 这条斜线已经守不住了：如果12... Be7，则13. Bxe7 Nxe7 14. dxc5 Qxd3 15. Qxe7；12... f6 13. Bc4+ Kh8 14. Bh6同样不能接受¹。

text: ¹ It is hard to see why this latter line is unacceptable. Black may continue with 14... Re8, threatening 15... Re4, and thanks to the move ...f6 Black's kingside dark squares are not especially weak.
zh: ¹ 很难看出后一条变化为什么不能接受。黑方可以接着14... Re8，威胁15... Re4；而且由于走过...f6，黑方王翼的黑格并不特别弱。

text: 13. O-O cxd4 14. cxd4 (D)
zh: 13. O-O cxd4 14. cxd4 (D)
caption_zh: 白方走完14. cxd4后的局面

text: Some commentators have marked this move out as the decisive mistake and have suggested 14... Be6 (preventing Bc4), but this would make the win easier, e.g. 15. Bf6 Rfe8 (or 15... h5 16. Qg5 Kh7 17. d5 Bxd5 18. Bxf5) 16. Nf4! Nxd4 (precluding 17. d5; if 16... Bxf4 17. Qxf4, Black will find himself unable to defend the focal-point g7, having given up his dark-squared bishop) 17. Nh5 Nc6 18. Bc3 Be5 (18... Be7 comes to the same) 19. Nf6+ Bxf6 20. Bxf6 h5 21. Qg5 Kh7 22. Be2 and White decides the game by Bxh5.
zh: 有些评注者把这步标为决定性的错误，并建议14... Be6，阻止Bc4。但那样白方赢得更容易，例如15. Bf6 Rfe8（或15... h5 16. Qg5 Kh7 17. d5 Bxd5 18. Bxf5）16. Nf4! Nxd4（阻止17. d5；如果16... Bxf4 17. Qxf4，黑方交出了黑格象，就会发现自己无法防守g7焦点）17. Nh5 Nc6 18. Bc3 Be5（18... Be7也一样）19. Nf6+ Bxf6 20. Bxf6 h5 21. Qg5 Kh7 22. Be2，白方用Bxh5决定胜负。

text: In this analysis, as in other phases of this game, it should be noted that a method has been used which we have already seen in the variations arising from the diagram on page 109; namely, in creating threats against a dark-square network, White repeatedly makes use of sacrifices on squares of the other colour. These sacrifices fulfil the task of breaking up clusters of pawns which otherwise impede the attacker's access to the weak squares on the network itself. The linkage between the operations on the networks of different colours should be noted; on one network the intention is to keep the attacking pieces in the strongest and most permanent positions possible, while on the other they are sacrificed when the situation demands.
zh: 应当注意，这段分析与本局其他阶段一样，采用了原书第109页局面的变化中已经出现过的方法：在对黑格网络制造威胁时，白方反复在另一颜色的格子上弃子。这些弃子的任务，是打散阻碍进攻方接近弱格网络的兵群。要注意，两种颜色格子上的行动彼此相连：在一种颜色上，进攻方力求让棋子占据尽可能强大、持久的位置；在另一种颜色上，则在局面需要时弃掉它们。

text: It should finally be pointed out that, instead of the move played, 14... Qxb2? would have been bad because of 15. Rfb1 Qa3 16. Rb3 Qa5 17. Bf6 Re8 18. Bc4, when White's prospects for an attack are greatly improved.
zh: 最后还应指出，如果不用实战走法，而走14... Qxb2?，也不好，因为15. Rfb1 Qa3 16. Rb3 Qa5 17. Bf6 Re8 18. Bc4，白方的进攻前景大为改善。

caption_zh: 黑方走完15... h5后的局面

text: There was a threat of 16. Bxf7+ Kxf7 17. Qh7+ Ke6 18. d5+ Kxd5 19. Rad1+. If 15... Be6, then 16. d5 would naturally follow.
zh: 白方原先威胁16. Bxf7+ Kxf7 17. Qh7+ Ke6 18. d5+ Kxd5 19. Rad1+。如果15... Be6，白方自然接着16. d5。

text: After this move Black gains drawing chances. In such an attractive position one would expect to find a safe and clear way to victory. White here has all the necessary ingredients for success: control over a dark-square network; advantage in development; two pieces to break up the cluster on the light squares (bishop at c4 and knight at e2); and as well as all this, a pawn in the centre that prevents Black from using his e5 square as a post for his pieces!
zh: 这步之后，黑方有了争取和棋的机会。在这样令人心动的局面中，人们会期待找到一条稳妥清楚的获胜道路。白方具备成功所需的全部条件：控制黑格网络；有出子优势；有两个棋子可以打散白格上的兵群，也就是c4象和e2马；此外，中心还有一个兵，阻止黑方把e5用作棋子的据点！

text: Stronger and simpler would have been 16. Bf6!, as the following lines show:
zh: 更强也更简单的是16. Bf6!，以下变化可以说明：

text: 2) 16... Be6 17. d5 Bxd5 18. Bxd5 Rxe2 19. Qg5 Kf8 20. Rae1!¹ Qb5 (or 20... Nd4 21. Qh6+ Ke8 22. Bxc6, etc.) 21. Bf3 Rxe1 22. Rxe1 Ne5 23. Qh6+ Ke8 24. Bxe5 and 25. Qh8+.
zh: 2）16... Be6 17. d5 Bxd5 18. Bxd5 Rxe2 19. Qg5 Kf8 20. Rae1!¹ Qb5（或20... Nd4 21. Qh6+ Ke8 22. Bxc6等）21. Bf3 Rxe1 22. Rxe1 Ne5 23. Qh6+ Ke8 24. Bxe5，接着25. Qh8+。

text: ¹ This move is refuted by 20... Qxf2+!! and Black forces mate himself. However, Vuković's attacking plan is basically correct, except that White has to exercise a little more care: 20. Qh6+ Ke8 21. Qg7 Nd8 22. Rae1 and now 22... Qxf2+ 23. Rxf2 Rxe1+ 24. Rf1 Bc5+ fails, because after 25. Bd4 the bishop is defended.
zh: ¹ 这步会被20... Qxf2+!!反驳，反而是黑方强制将杀。不过，武科维奇的进攻计划基本正确，只是白方必须更谨慎一些：20. Qh6+ Ke8 21. Qg7 Nd8 22. Rae1。现在22... Qxf2+ 23. Rxf2 Rxe1+ 24. Rf1 Bc5+不行了，因为25. Bd4之后，白象有保护。

text: 3) 16... Re4 17. Qg5 Kf8 18. Nc3!, and the black rook has no good square to go to: 18... Rxd4 is inadequate because of 19. Rfe1, while 18... Rg4 is answered by 19. Qh6+ Ke8 20. Bxf7+ Kxf7 21. Qg7+ Ke8 (or 21... Ke6 22. d5#) 22. Rae1+ and mate is unavoidable.
zh: 3）16... Re4 17. Qg5 Kf8 18. Nc3!，黑车无处可去：18... Rxd4不够，因为有19. Rfe1；18... Rg4则应以19. Qh6+ Ke8 20. Bxf7+ Kxf7 21. Qg7+ Ke8（或21... Ke6 22. d5#）22. Rae1+，将杀不可避免。

text: 16... Re4 17. Nf4 Qxd4 18. Rxe4 fxe4?
zh: 16... Re4 17. Nf4 Qxd4 18. Rxe4 fxe4?

text: This pawn blocks the fourth rank to White's advantage. Black should have played 18... Qxe4, when 19. Nxg6 Qxh4 20. Nxh4 leads to an ending in which White is the better placed, but Black can still salvage a draw by 20... Be6 21. Bd3 (or 21. Be2 Kg7! when 22. Bxh5 fails against 22... f6 and 23... Rh8) 21... f4 threatening both the a-pawn and 22... Kg7 followed by 23... f6.
zh: 这个兵堵住了第四横线，对白方有利。黑方应走18... Qxe4，19. Nxg6 Qxh4 20. Nxh4之后进入白方较好的残局，但黑方仍可用20... Be6 21. Bd3（或21. Be2 Kg7!，此时22. Bxh5会遭到22... f6，接着23... Rh8）21... f4争取和棋，既威胁a兵，也威胁22... Kg7，接着23... f6。

text: Breaking up Black's light-square complex.
zh: 打散黑方在白格上的兵群。

text: Forced; if 20... Qxc4 then White wins by 21. Qxh5 while if 20... Be5 then 21. Qg5+ is decisive.
zh: 被迫如此；如果20... Qxc4，白方走21. Qxh5获胜；如果20... Be5，则21. Qg5+决定胜负。

caption_zh: 黑方走完21... Kf8后的局面

text: The only reply. If 21... Be6 then 22. Rd5! Qxc4 (or 22... Bxd5 23. Qxh5) 23. Qg5+ Kf8 24. Rxd6 and mates, while 21... Be7 22. Rd5 Bxf6 loses to 23. Qg3+.
zh: 唯一应招。如果21... Be6，则22. Rd5! Qxc4（或22... Bxd5 23. Qxh5）23. Qg5+ Kf8 24. Rxd6，将杀；21... Be7 22. Rd5 Bxf6则会被23. Qg3+击败。

text: Obliging the knight to abandon its watch on d8. That White's bishop on c4 is still 'taboo' can be seen from 22... Qxc4 23. Qxh5 Ke8 24. Rxd6 Qc1+ 25. Rd1, and Black loses his queen.
zh: 迫使马放弃对d8的看守。白方c4象仍然“吃不得”，以下变化可以说明：22... Qxc4 23. Qxh5 Ke8 24. Rxd6 Qc1+ 25. Rd1，黑方失后。

text: Clearly the only answer, for 23... Bxg3 cannot be played on account of 24. Rd8#.
zh: 显然是唯一应招，因为有24. Rd8#，黑方不能走23... Bxg3。

text: 24. Rxd6 Nd3
zh: 24. Rxd6 Nd3

text: Or 24... Qxc4 25. Qf4 and mates.
zh: 或24... Qxc4 25. Qf4，将杀。

text: 25. Bxd3 Qc1+
zh: 25. Bxd3 Qc1+

text: Not 25... exd3 because of 26. Qf4.
zh: 不能走25... exd3，因为有26. Qf4。

text: 26. Bf1 Rc8 27. h3 Qxf1+ 28. Kh2! Qc1 29. hxg4 hxg4 30. Qxg4 Qh6+ 31. Kg3 Rc3+ 32. f3 1-0
zh: 26. Bf1 Rc8 27. h3 Qxf1+ 28. Kh2! Qc1 29. hxg4 hxg4 30. Qxg4 Qh6+ 31. Kg3 Rc3+ 32. f3 1-0

text: The first part of this tense game is instructive as an example of the gradual creation of the preconditions necessary for an attack on the castled king, while from the twelfth move onwards, by which time White's control of the dark-square network is assured, the course of the game and its analysis provide many useful lessons on how to carry out an attack of this kind.
zh: 这盘紧张对局的前半部很有启发性，展示了如何逐步创造攻击王城所需的前提。从第12步起，白方对黑格网络的控制已经确立，此后的实战进程及分析，则对如何实施这种攻击提供了许多有益的启示。
